title: Notifications: All Apps, mixed while they differ
caption: Preferences ▸ Notifications' Applications table has an All Apps row over the list: each column checked when every app's is, a dash while they differ (the kit's CheckBox::mixed); a click sets it for every app. With the Deskbar box above it, the panel is taller.

title: New windows glow a moment (Preferences ▸ Appearance)
caption: With Glow new windows for N seconds on (off by default, 5 s), a new window has a soft halo in the look's focus blue round its frame and tab as one shape, fading out over its last second; left: just opened, right: after (at 1×, enlarged 2×).

title: Token Pool: the Clients window
caption: Pool ▸ Clients: the pool's activity over time (requests a minute by client, over the last hour, six hours or day, with totals), Codex's service with its version, settings, connections, conversations and Restart, and each Claude Code and Codex running and where its connections go (here a sandbox with a made-up day of activity).

title: Window menu: every display's workspaces
caption: A window's tab menu ▸ Move to Workspace lists every display's workspaces, left to right as Deskbar names them, its own display's with their keys and a check; another display's moves it there, to the same place, tiled or zoomed as it was.

title: Deskbar: an app's windows to any workspace
caption: An app's Deskbar menu moves its windows as a tab's menu moves one: Move to Workspace ▸ every display's workspaces (the one they're on checked), and To the Next / Previous Display.

title: Deskbar: every display's workspaces, and the display's number
caption: Each Deskbar lists every display's workspaces and their apps, its own display's first (here D1's Deskbar, then D0's), and its tray shows its display's number in a small monitor; clicking it lists the displays and goes to the one chosen.

title: Terminal: Tile All Tabs, a row per group
caption: Tile All Tabs (was Show All Tabs) gives each group a row, its tabs side by side, and the ungrouped tabs a row of their own; clicking groups' chips chooses which tile (lit as Deskbar's workspace showing): here alpha and beta of three, a row each; one alone fills a grid; the right button gives the group's menu.

title: Preferences ▸ Terminal: Coding Agents
caption: Tell coding agents about the repositories in their tab group (off by default): Claude Code and Codex in a tab of a group spanning repositories are told the group's name and its repositories and worktrees, through their own hooks.

title: Notifications: only the latest of the same
caption: Preferences ▸ Notifications ▸ History: Only the latest of the same notification (on by default): the same again from the same app takes the earlier one's place while it's still showing or unread.

title: Agent Screens: History follows the agent live
caption: Agent Screens revamped: a sidebar of running and stopped screens, a header saying how the chosen one is, and Live, History and Stats tabs. History now follows the history as it's written (each new action chosen and shown as it comes), its scroll bar works (the list was pinned to the playhead's row every frame), and a search with Kind, Result and Time filters narrows it; under the picture, what the action did.

title: Agent Screens: filters
caption: History's filters, as Log Viewer's: Result ▸ Failed keeps the 12 of 249 actions that failed, each with why in red.

title: Agent Screens: Stats
caption: Stats as dashboard cards (dark, 1.5×): use, actions by kind, actions a minute over the last hour, programs run.

title: Terminal: Tile All Tabs rows' heights dragged
caption: In Tile All Tabs, the line between two groups' rows (and the heads under it) drags their heights; the shares go by group and are kept with the window. The right button there gives the group's menu with Reset Row Heights.

title: Performance supervisor: Activity Monitor's Supervisor section and Preferences ▸ Performance
caption: The supervisor (off by default) lowers builds and background work and watches for stuck processes, leaks, memory hogs and zombies, each judged from several signals with a confidence and evidence. Activity Monitor shows it as cards (Inspect, Stop Process, Ignore This Process); every threshold is tuned in Preferences ▸ Performance.

title: Performance supervisor, dark
caption: The same in the dark look: the findings' confidence in the failure colour.

title: Supervisor alert, sized for its buttons
caption: An urgent finding asks in an alert naming the process, what was found and the evidence. The kit's WindowOptions::alert_buttons widens an alert to fit long button labels.

title: Inspector: the Supervisor tab
caption: A process's inspector has a Supervisor tab: its findings, how sure and why, and whether it was lowered and why. The alert's Show in Activity Monitor opens it there.

title: Deskbar: the supervisor's gauge at 1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, 1.75×, 2×
caption: On (dial tinted, needle up, the findings counted, red if urgent) and off (dim, needle resting). A click turns it on or off; its menu lists the findings, Show in Activity Monitor and Performance Settings…

title: Terminal: a coding agent's title for its tab
caption: With Preferences ▸ Terminal's new setting, Claude Code and Codex get a set_tab_title tool (an MCP server of Terminal's) and are asked to keep their tab titled with what they're working on; here the tool was called from the tab.

title: Preferences ▸ Terminal: Let coding agents keep their tab's title current
caption: Off by default; the panel is taller for it.

title: Quick Look full screen on two displays: before
caption: Quick Look on the right display, F: it filled the left display (the first one), and on the right it hung off its old place at full-screen size.

title: Quick Look full screen on two displays: after
caption: F fills only the display the window is on; the other is untouched, and F again puts it back where it was. Same at 1.5× and 2×.

title: StyledEdit: paragraph styles and lists
caption: Paragraphs have a style (Title, Heading 1-3, Quote, Code, Body), bulleted and numbered lists that nest and number themselves, indents and their own alignment; the kit's editor sets each paragraph's indents, spacing and list marker (Document::paragraph). Word count in the status line.

title: StyledEdit: spelling as you type
caption: Misspelled words get a red wave under them (the kit editor's Options::spelling, Hunspell dictionaries read natively by spellbook); right-click one for suggestions, Ignore Spelling or Learn Spelling.

title: Printing: the Print panel and PDF
caption: StyledEdit's File > Print... (and Export > PDF): a printer from CUPS (spoken to natively over IPP) or a PDF, paper, copies and pages; pages laid out as the editor lays them out and made into a PDF in process (krilla), fonts embedded, text selectable.

title: StyledEdit: tables
caption: A paragraph can be a table's row: its cells its text between tabs, laid out side by side in columns by the kit editor and ruled a device pixel wide (a header row shaded). Tab and ⇧Tab go from cell to cell, Tab in the last cell and Return add a row, and edits keep a table's cells and rows. The Table menu inserts and converts tables, adds and deletes rows and columns, and toggles the header; Word, OpenDocument, RTF and Markdown tables come in as tables and go out as them.

title: File panels: Kind column, sorting, Favorites and Recent Folders
caption: Every Open and Save panel lists Name, Kind, Size and Modified, sorted by any of them (folders first, names in natural order); the folder pop-up has the folders above this one, the standard places, Favorites (add or remove this folder) and Recent Folders, kept in ~/.config/olo/places.json and shared with Tracker's Go menu. Space looks at the selected file in the Viewer, as Quick Look.

title: StyledEdit: dragging a table's column rule
caption: A table's inner rule can be dragged: a line shows where it will go, and let go, every row of the table takes the new widths (one step to undo). The widths are kept in StyledEdit's own files and in Word, OpenDocument, RTF and HTML.

title: StyledEdit: the ruler, indents and tab stops
caption: A ruler over the text (the kit's ruler; Document ▸ Show Ruler): the caret's paragraph's first-line, left and right indents to drag, and tab stops: a click sets one, a drag moves it or takes it off, and its menu (or a double click) makes it left, centre, right or decimal. Tabs now go to stops (epaint's TabStops); here a left stop at 1½ in and a decimal one at 2¼ in line up a price list. Indents and stops are kept in Word, OpenDocument and RTF.

title: StyledEdit: Header & Footer
caption: Document ▸ Header & Footer… sets a left, centre and right part above and below every printed page, {page} and {pages} standing for the page number and count. Kept in the file, and in Word, OpenDocument and RTF (checked in LibreOffice).

title: StyledEdit: pictures
caption: Pictures in the text: Insert Picture…, pasted or dropped; drawn by the kit's editor where their character is, sized from the Edit menu, kept beside the document, and in Word, OpenDocument, RTF, web pages, Markdown and print.

title: StyledEdit: Page View
caption: Document ▸ Page View sets the text on sheets of the paper it prints on, with its margins: paragraphs and rows break across pages as printed, headers and footers on each sheet; the kit editor's Options::pages.

title: StyledEdit: Page View, dark
caption: The desk half way to black under dark sheets.

title: Telegram: polls and reactions on their baselines
caption: A poll's shares stand on their answers' baseline; a reaction's count is centred in its chip by its figures with the emoji on their middle, and the emoji lines up with the message text above. Voice notes' waveform bars and the file glyph sit on device pixels at every scale. The layout review now judges an emoji inside a line of text with that line, not against the whole bubble.

title: Preferences ▸ Display: each display's panel
caption: What the display is (make, size, density, refresh), what Olo works out about its panel (technology, colour stripes) and how it draws text on it, with why, each correctable (Automatic or a choice). Shown on a simulated 24-inch 1080p LCD (92 ppi): subpixel text.

title: GPUI kit: the column list view
caption: olo-ui gains BColumnListView (right), as the egui kit draws it (left, the demo's Lists tab): header sorting and dividers, the file-manager selection (shared now as olo_kit_base::list), bands, type-select, BeOS scroll bars; at 1.5x, where GPUI windows had been drawn at 2x and shrunk (fixed here).

title: Token Pool on GPUI
caption: Token Pool moves to olo-ui: the same window (gateway, now-grid, client switches, account cards with quota bars and request strips, Account menu, rename), drawn by GPUI. A test account in a fixture home; 73.6 MB against egui's 91.9 MB, idle with no wakeups.

title: DiskUsage on GPUI
caption: DiskUsage moves to the GPUI kit (olo-ui): the ring chart's slices are GPU sectors (paint_sector) with hairlines over them, the list beside it a ColumnListView whose rows drag into the Collector, Volumes, menus with the keyboard profile's keys, alerts and the folder panel all as before. The chart redraws only when the slice under the pointer changes, in about a millisecond; the list's name column now fits inside its scroll bar (egui's cut Files off), and the Collector's chips show each file's kind.

title: Screenshot on GPUI
caption: Screenshot moves to the GPUI kit: the same form and buttons, the preview made at exactly its frame's size in device pixels (remade when the scale changes) and drawn one pixel to a pixel, Copy to clipboard as image/png through GPUI's clipboard (which now offers images and data, not only text), Save closing the window and holding the path on the clipboard until something else is copied. The ⌘⇧4 region picker and the colour picker are GPUI layer overlays showing each output's frozen picture 1:1.

title: DriveSetup on GPUI
caption: DriveSetup moves to the GPUI kit: the disk map (segments to scale, hatched free space, the unlocked contents under a purple band) over the list of disks and volumes, the status line with progress and Stop, and its forms (Format, Create with a size slider, Resize, Rename, Unlock, New Partition Table) as alert windows that grow and shrink with their fields. Here on the test UDisks (udisks-fake). The kit gains BeOS keyboard navigation for it: Tab moves through fields, lists and controls (the focused control's label underlined in blue, Space presses it), and a default button answers Return from anywhere in its window.

title: The command palette on GPUI
caption: The command palette, its window menu and the shortcuts sheet move to the GPUI kit. Same look; key symbols (⇧ ⌘ ↵) set on the capitals' line by their outlines, the subtitle and kind on the title's baseline, the query lined up with the titles. It opens in 28 ms (egui: 47) and holds 40 MB less; small text's darkening is now an emboldened outline rather than a stroke (the same look, a third of the time).

title: Log Viewer on GPUI
caption: Log Viewer moves to the GPUI kit, with the kit's new search field (filters coloured, suggested as they're typed), filter bar and text view; the Message column now fits beside the scroll bar (no sideways scrolling). Loading 160,000 lines its slowest frame is 3 ms (egui's 34). A made-up log file, not a real journal.

title: Google Chrome's installer on GPUI
caption: The offer to download Google Chrome (shown when it isn't installed) moves to the GPUI kit, now with its installer icon, which the egui window never found. 54 MB against 77.

title: Deskbar on GPUI
caption: Deskbar moves to Olo's GPUI kit: the same tile, tray and workspaces, drawn on device pixels at every scale (the tray's glyphs as exact paths and GPU arcs), its menus' keys laid out as the egui kit's key combos, tips in popups of their own, applications dragged out as links with their icon and name. 57 MB against 141, and 32 frames for 30 pointer moves against 150.

title: Telegram on GPUI
caption: Telegram moves to the GPUI kit: the same list, conversation and composer (a multi-line field: Return sends, Shift-Return a new line), its panes cached views of their own so a hover, a scroll or the caret redraws only its pane. Shown: the demo account's forum with topics, a reply, code and a photo, at 2x.

title: Menus without stray separators
caption: A menu built with items it shows only sometimes (Telegram's Chat menu with no chat open) ended in a separator with nothing under it; the GPUI kit now leaves out separators at either end of a menu and two together.

title: Viewer on GPUI
caption: The Viewer moved to the GPUI kit: pictures fitted and resampled exactly to the device size on a worker, zoomed in tiles; the crop frame drawn over the picture, its thirds while it moves and its size under it; PDF forms, text boxes, ink and signatures; formatted documents, sheets, code, archives, fonts, sound and video from olo-preview's GPUI views. Windows open sized for the display they open on.

title: Notifications on GPUI
caption: Notifications, banners and History, now on Olo's GPUI: the same cards, groups, stop signs, balloons and reply fields, with words kept on a row when they fit (spaces hang past the edge, as egui and typesetters wrap), the generic application icon for apps without one in banners and History alike, and an exact gap after an error's stop sign. 61 MB against egui's 153 with four banners; History scrolls 200 notes at 1.3–1.8 ms a frame.

title: The share picker on GPUI
caption: olo-portal's dialogs move to the GPUI kit: the share picker (live thumbnails in the kit's new ThumbnailPicker), permission, wallpaper, shortcuts and Open With questions, and the file and Print panels, each over the asking app's window by xdg-foreign. Its thumbnails no longer pile up in the GPU's atlas; a permission dialog opens in ~8 ms.

title: Agent Screens on GPUI
caption: Agent Screens moved to Olo's GPUI: the sidebar, header and Live/History/Stats tabs as before, now with the kit's GPUI Sidebar, TabView and dashboard cards. Live takes a picture only when the screen draws something new (app_server's new Painted event), each resampled to the exact device size on a worker; History plays back drawing only what changes.

title: Activity Monitor on GPUI
caption: Activity Monitor moves from egui to Olo's GPUI kit, looking as it did. Its window is cached parts with the section's graphs on a layer of their own (the kit's GraphLayer): a graph moving a pixel redraws the graphs, not the cards around them. Graphs' fills are a new GPU primitive (paint_area) instead of paths filled through window-sized multisampled textures, and a window's graphs move together on one clock. On release at 2×: the UI thread at or under egui's in every section with graphs (CPU 3.9% of a core against 5.2), 93–96 MB against 119–123.

title: Passwords on GPUI
caption: Passwords moves to the GPUI kit: its panes are cached parts of the window, so a one-time code counting down redraws the item pane alone, once a second; half the CPU of the egui version in every interaction and 90 MB against 124. Synthetic items from the test 1Password.

title: Activity Monitor ▸ Displays
caption: Each display's frames a second, the ones dropped (a vblank or more late), what its frames cost app_server to draw and how app_server paces them (frames.rs: the draw's share of the frame set from its cost and from drops), whether the pointer is on a plane of its own; and the check box that has every drop logged with what went into it. Made-up displays here (OLO_ACTIVITY_DEMO_FRAMES); a headless session has none.

title: Olo Doctor
caption: A new app that looks the computer over for what gets in Olo's way (an input remapper grabbing the mice, USB receivers allowed to sleep, Olo's udev rules missing, rtkit down, another desktop's daemons, programs on an old version) and fixes each with a button, or all at once with one password.

title: Mice by make and model
caption: Preferences ▸ Touchpad & Mouse ▸ Mouse names each mouse by maker and model (sensor, resolution, how it's connected), offers the profile recommended for it or settings of its own, says what is known about it, and points at Olo Doctor for what gets in its way (a key remapper grabbing it, a receiver allowed to sleep). The device list now comes by event, not every 3 s.

title: Screen saver on GPUI
caption: olo-screensaver draws on Olo's GPUI: Message, Icons, Lissart, Lens and Spots (rows) at 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 and 2× (columns), over a test desktop. Lens magnifies the desktop through textured triangles, Lissart's hundreds of lines are painted a layer at a time.

title: StyledEdit on GPUI
caption: StyledEdit moves to the GPUI kit: its editor, ruler and spelling are olo-ui's now. Page View with a header, a table and a picture at 2x. Scrolls, types and resizes within a 120 Hz frame at every scale on a full 16-inch screen, as evenly as egui did; ends stretch and spring back.

title: Tracker on GPUI
caption: Tracker moved from the egui kit to Olo's GPUI: folder windows (icons, mini icons, list, columns), the desktop, Get Info, Find, Tracker Status and Quick Look, with BeOS's drag rules through GPUI's own drops and Paste read off the UI thread.

title: Pinch to zoom, off by default
caption: Preferences ▸ Touchpad & Mouse ▸ Gestures: a pinch reaches the window under the pointer only when this is on. Off, two fingers drifting together while scrolling no longer zoom Chrome's pages.

title: Preferences on GPUI
caption: Every panel of Preferences moved from egui to Olo's GPUI, drawn as before; Themes shows each theme's wordmark and icons, and its colour sets now share their row evenly.

title: Terminal's tabs, redesigned
caption: Terminal on GPUI with a new tab strip (olo-ui's TabStrip): everything sits inside the band. Tabs are their titles; the selected one is on a raised plate lit from above (a touch lighter at the top, its rim's top edge lit and tapering into the corners, a soft shadow), as BeOS lit its controls. A group is a capsule of its colour around its chip and tabs, with corners concentric with the plates inside. No lines, and nothing rises above the strip. Each tab is as wide as its title needs.

title: Terminal's tabs in light mode
caption: The same strip in light mode: a white plate on the quiet band, each group's capsule at 16% of its colour (22% in the dark).

title: Terminal's Tile All Tabs heads
caption: In Tile All Tabs each pane's head is on the strip's quiet band, with its group's chip at the right instead of a tint and a coloured line. The pane you type in has its title in full ink and medium weight, like the strip's selected tab. Icon, title and chip are centred on the band to the device pixel at every scale.

title: Picture in picture stays in its corner
caption: A call popped out of Chrome (documentPictureInPicture, as Meet does) opens in the bottom right corner at its own size, over every window and on each workspace, out of Chrome's group, Focus's zoom and the window memory; the keyboard stays where it was. A link opened from another app (Terminal's Open Pull Request) now shows in Chrome, in front, with the call over it: before, the call joined Chrome's group and zoomed over the tab the link had opened in.

title: A video's picture in picture, Standard mode
caption: Chrome's video picture in picture (no app id, titled "Picture in picture") in the corner, 16 px in, over the call page's window.

title: AirPods panel
caption: Preferences ▸ AirPods: levels with a picture of each bud and the case, noise control with Adaptive's strength, press and hold, listening features, the microphone, and what this computer does with them. Shown with a pretend pair (OLO_FAKE_AIRPODS).

title: AirPods panel, dark, 1×
caption: The same at 1× in dark mode.

title: Sound: AirPods
caption: Preferences ▸ Sound with AirPods as the output: their model, codec and whether they play at music or call quality, noise control, and where to record from while they're connected.

title: Deskbar: AirPods
caption: Deskbar's tray shows AirPods while they're connected (amber or red when a bud runs low); its menu has their levels, noise control, Conversation Awareness and their settings.

title: AirPods icons in every theme
caption: airpods, airpods-case, airpod-left and airpod-right, generated against each theme's references (Classic, BeBox, Soft Be, Toybox, Papercraft, Enamel, Halftone), beside bluetooth and sound.

title: Preferences on a short screen
caption: A panel taller than the screen (AirPods, 752 points, on a 700-point display) opens as tall as fits, laid out at its own size and scrolled, with a scroll bar the window is widened for. Panels that fit are unchanged.

title: Tracker: Go to File or Folder
caption: Go ▸ Go to File or Folder… (⇧⌘G): a path copied is in the field already, selected, so Return goes; the names in its folder that what's typed could be are listed as it's typed, Tab completes, ↑↓ choose. A folder opens; a file shows selected in its folder's window.

title: Deskbar: the speaker's menu
caption: Right-click the speaker: every output and input, mute, and while AirPods play, their levels, noise control, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, music or call quality, and both settings panels.

title: Command palette: every setting in Preferences
caption: Each control in every Preferences panel is a palette result, named with its panel, tab and box, and found by the words people use for it elsewhere ('night shift' finds Night Mode). The index is made from the panels as they're drawn, so a new setting is found without listing it.

title: A setting found is shown, lit
caption: Chosen in the palette, Preferences opens the setting's panel (on its tab, clicked if need be) with the control ringed in the keyboard-navigation colour for a moment: olo_ui::spotlight, which any app or agent can use to say 'here'. Two lines wide on device pixels; frames only while it comes and goes.

title: Command palette: Go to the path in the clipboard
caption: With a path copied (absolute, ~/…, a file:// URI), the palette offers to go there before anything is typed, and a path typed whole is offered too: Tracker shows it, a folder in its window, a file selected in its folder's. Read off the UI thread once the palette has the keyboard, which app_server now gives an exclusive layer as it shows.

title: Text cut short shows whole in a tip
caption: Resting the pointer on text the kit cut with … (here a name in Tracker's column) shows all of it in the kit's tip; with ⌘ held, at once. Every kit window does it for every label it cuts or that runs past its clip.

title: A window tab's cut title shows whole
caption: app_server shows the whole title of a window whose tab cuts it short on a tooltip's plate under the tab, once the pointer rests on the title (at once with ⌘), as Olo's apps do for their cut text.

title: Terminal: text kept legible on any background
caption: Before (top) and after: colours a program picked for a dark terminal (pale greys and blues, bright white) or bands it drew (diff lines, a composer's grey) left text nearly invisible in light mode. Now text keeps WCAG's 4.5:1 against its cell, moved toward black or white just as far as it takes, its hue kept; box drawing and blocks as drawn; faint text still faint.

title: Tracker: Open With and Always Open With
caption: A file's menu offers a few apps that suit its kind (its default marked, Olo's own, then those that say they open it), and Always Open With makes one the kind's default for Olo and for other programs.

title: Preferences: Default Apps
caption: A new panel: each kind of file and link with the app it opens in, changeable from the apps that suit it; a choice is the kind's for Olo and for other programs (Tracker's Always Open With chooses too). Its icon, a document with Olo's application cube, from the reference set.

title: Tracker: Open With ▸ Other…
caption: Any app can open a file: Other… lists every app that opens files, found by typing part of its name, with 'Always open files like … with it'.

title: Default Apps: your own kinds
caption: Preferences ▸ Default Apps ▸ Your Own Kinds: a kind named by its extensions (Game saves: .sav .sv2) opens in the app chosen; Olo knows files by it everywhere (olo_xdg::mime::own_kinds).

title: Default Apps: what Open With offers
caption: The Open With tab: a kind's apps in Open With ▸, in order, moved, removed and added; Olo's Choice lets Olo choose again.

title: File panels: Open With
caption: An item's menu in the Open and Save panels: Quick Look, Open With ▸ (the kit's olo_ui::open_with, as Tracker's) and Show in Tracker.

title: Sound: Voice Processing
caption: Every microphone through Olo's voice processing (echo cancellation, DeepFilterNet noise suppression, level), and what it is doing now, in a line. Here against a sandboxed sound server's made-up devices.

title: Deskbar: voice processing in the speaker's menu
caption: Right-click the speaker: Clean Up Microphone Sound, and in a submenu what it's tuned for, how much background noise to take out, echo and level (through olo-voice --set, as an agent would).

title: Focus: an alert from a covered app shows
caption: In Focus mode an alert that names no window (here StyledEdit's 'Save changes?' while Tracker is in front; Passwords' passkey question over Chrome) shows over the window in front, with the keyboard, instead of staying hidden with its app.

title: File panel: the look floats
caption: Space in a file panel (here the portal's, as Slack asks) looks at the file in a floating window over the panel, never a tile.

title: Telegram: Unknown Senders
caption: People who aren't contacts and were never written to get a list of their own under the archive: no notification, no unread count, until written back to. Avatars are 40 pt, from 46.

title: Telegram: chats chosen together
caption: ⌘-click, ⇧-click or Edit ▸ Select All Chats chooses several; their menu archives, unarchives, marks read, mutes or deletes them all (asking first).

title: Olo Suggestions
caption: A new app: what Olo suggests, none of it needed, each applied with a button or all with Apply All. The first: brush, the bash-compatible shell in Rust, as the login shell.

title: Olo Suggestions: applied, and undone
caption: What's applied is listed with a button that undoes it (here: Use bash Again).

title: Menus taller than the screen scroll
caption: A kit menu longer than its display stops short of its edges and scrolls: an arrow at each end there's more past scrolls it while the pointer rests there; the wheel and the keys too. Here Default Apps' every app, at the top and scrolled to the end.

title: Banners over Deskbar's menu (before)
caption: Before: a notification banner, a Top layer surface that came after Deskbar, drew over Deskbar's menus and took their clicks.

title: Deskbar's menus over banners
caption: Layer surfaces' menus are drawn and hit-tested over the whole Top layer, so Deskbar's menus are over any banner (shell::layer_menus).

title: Quick Look from a file panel (before)
caption: Before: the look, a process of its own with no parent, opened in a cascade slot at the asking app's corner, half over the panel.

title: Quick Look centred over the file panel
caption: The panel exports its window (xdg-foreign, Window::export_handle) and the Viewer opens the look over it (--over=); app_server keeps a dialog that sizes itself after opening centred over its parent until it's moved.

title: Agent Screens: a screen renamed
caption: Screen ▸ Rename… or a click on its title: the name the person gives shows in the list and the header, kept with its history (olo-screen rename NAME TITLE; list says it).

title: Agent Screens: several chosen, archived, deleted
caption: ⌘- and ⇧-clicks or ⌘A choose screens together; their menu archives, unarchives, stops or deletes them all (asked once); View ▸ Show Archived lists the archived in their own section; Delete moves histories to the Trash.

title: Emoji picker: five from AI for a description
caption: ⌃⌘Space opens the emoji picker over everything: search as you type, a tab a group, skin tones kept; ⌘↩ asks the model chosen in Preferences ▸ AI for five emoji for what was typed, each with its reason. Return puts the selected one into the field that had the keyboard, in any app (app_server's InsertText). (A fake model answered here; tests never call a real one.)

title: Preferences ▸ AI: Emoji
caption: The emoji picker's AI suggestions get their own switch, model and effort (low by default: they're asked while you wait), as Smart Tiling has; the panel grows to fit them.

title: Telegram: changes kept until Telegram has them
caption: Archiving, reading, muting and pinning go into an outbox on disk and leave it only once Telegram has them, sent again on the next start if need be. A line under the chat list shows them going; quitting waits up to 30 s for them (Quit Now quits at once; what's left is kept). The demo account, its changes slowed down to show it.

title: Agent Screens: Live at the screen's own frame rate
caption: Live now shows the agent screen's own frames, shared with the person's compositor as dmabufs (a subsurface of the window), at up to 120 frames a second; before, it took up to eight pictures a second and resampled each on the CPU (30% of a core while the screen moved, 0.6% now). The frame line round the picture stays flush at every scale.

title: Preferences ▸ Terminal: tell coding agents to use Agent Screens
caption: A third Coding Agents setting: Claude Code and Codex are told as they start to test and use desktop apps and web pages on Agent Screens of their own, and how, Olo's Chrome included, so they never start a Chrome on the person's screen. The panel is taller to fit it.

title: Text fields scroll to the caret, and show cut text in a tip
caption: A one-line field used to always show its start: typing past its end hid the caret and what was typed (top, before). Now it scrolls sideways while edited, keeping the caret in view (middle). Unfocused, it shows its start again, and the whole text is in a tip on hover (bottom). Never a password's.

title: Preferences ▸ Touchpad ▸ Touch: Train for Your Palm
caption: A guided run through five exercises on the touchpad, each shown as an Olo-style animation of hands on a pad (left) and mirrored live by what the pad sees (right: a palm in orange, a finger in blue), with a word on how it's going and how many more touches it needs. Then Olo's hand-written palm model is refined to the person's hands off the UI thread, kept in the settings, and tried live.

title: Train for Your Palm, in a dialog of its own
caption: The palm trainer moved out of the Touch tab (where it ran off the panel) into a 560×440 dialog opened from a button. The film is a laptop's deck, keys and the pad between the palm rests, with the hands resting and lifting; beside it the pad live, its own shape, each touch drawn as the model calls it: here one hand's palm half over the left edge, which the size rule misses (the red ring) and the model catches. A sixth exercise gathers exactly that case.

title: StyledEdit's tool bars
caption: The kit's new ToolBar: StyledEdit's file, editing and format tools along the top (wrapping to two rows in a narrow window, a » menu for what still doesn't fit), insert and view tools down the side. Every tool is a menu command and shows its state (Bold and Center pushed for the selected title); the pickers show the font, size and colour where the selection starts. 25 new icons, in every theme.

title: Backup takes passwords to another computer
caption: Preferences ▸ Backup seals passwords and sign-ins into the backup with a password, and moves it in on another computer: paths under the new home, the Token Pool paused, Telegram signed in again; what an import left behind is listed.

title: Train for Your Palm: one thing a step, and a banner when it's done
caption: Each of the twelve exercises asks one thing, with a line under the title saying what to do now (rest, hold, point, lift) from the hands on the pad; a finished step gets a green banner in the place of the status line (the kit's new Banner), and the key caps sit level with their labels at every scale.

title: Sound ▸ Voice Processing ▸ Try It
caption: A few seconds of your voice, recorded and put through each setting worth comparing: what each adds (delay, its time a 10 ms frame, what noise suppression and levelling did) and what ran it; played as the original or the chosen setting's sound, switching at the same place, with a live spectrum of both (the kit's new Spectrum).

title: Terminal: tile mode's group headers selected while their groups show
caption: With every group tiled (the default), each group's header is drawn selected; a click takes that group out of the tiles and another brings it back.

title: Terminal: Hide When Tiled
caption: A tab's menu hides it from Tile All Tabs: it stays in the strip with its icon and title faded, and the tiles share the window without it.

title: Terminal: the side strip lined up
caption: Down the side, the tabs' icons, the groups' names and New Tab's + sit under the menu bar's first title, the first chip clears the menu bar as it does along the top, and the pane heads beside it are as tall as the top strip.

title: Command palette: every text key, and Ctrl for files
caption: Text editing's keys are commands of their own (Move to the end of the line, ⌘→), done in the window the palette opened over; files and folders come with a tap of Ctrl, as the key hint at the field's right says.

title: Terminal: a slim scroll bar, there when wanted
caption: The kit's SlimScrollBar over the scrollback's right edge: shown when the pointer comes near or the view scrolls, wider under the pointer, fading a moment after; its thumb drags and its track pages.

title: Terminal ▸ Command Suggestions: brush's hints from a model of your own
caption: Preferences ▸ Terminal turns on olo-complete, a tiny model of your own commands (the line, the folder, the commands before in that shell, the hour and the day) that gives brush its grey hint. Turning it on starts it and runs its first fine-tune from the history, then says how it did on your newest commands; it learns again a minute after you type. Unavailable while brush isn't the login shell, and a brush from before the model is told apart by a mark in its binary, each with a button to Olo Suggestions. The pane is 520×692 for its tallest state.

title: Activity Monitor ▸ AI: how the command model does
caption: A new section, asked of olo-complete once a second only while it shows: suggestions offered and taken (whole or a word at a time), what it knows, latency from the question to the answer sent (typically, 95th percentile, slowest) with a graph, and its learning: fine-tunes, the last one's examples, steps and time, how often its first suggestion is right on the newest commands against the hand-written weights, and whether it was kept. Off, it says so, with Terminal Preferences… to turn it on.

title: Display: settings beside the panel, the window as tall as both
caption: At 200 % on the ThinkPad's 3200 × 2000 panel, Display was a 658-point window scrolling an 804-point panel, its scroll bar against the boxes. Now the display's settings and its panel's facts are side by side, in a window that follows what it shows (fits_content), on every screen down to 1280 × 800.

title: Power: the power mode
caption: Performance, Balanced or Power Saver, through the power profiles daemon (tuned-ppd here): the processors' energy preference, the ThinkPad's platform profile. Also in Deskbar's battery menu; Performance has a button here.

title: Performance in two tabs, the thresholds two by two
caption: It was 1,220 points tall in a scroll view of its own; now Supervisor and Watchdog tabs, fitting a 1280 × 800 screen unscrolled.

title: Deskbar: Olo Doctor's bag in the tray
caption: Shown while Olo Doctor's last look (at login and every 15 minutes) found something to fix; a click opens it.

title: Fitting windows open at their size
caption: A window that fits what it shows (here Preferences ▸ Display, with its displays and GPUs, which come from app_server just after it opens) is no longer shown at its designed size and then grown: frames drawn at a size about to change aren't shown, and what it asks for as it opens holds its first showing for up to 150 ms. Display opens at 940×607 at once (before: 520, then 607). Its Graphics box's labels now level with their values.

title: Preferences ▸ GPUs
caption: A new panel: each GPU, what it drives, and its tuning. Presets (Cooler and Quieter, Balanced, Fastest) or the knobs by hand: Intel's lowest and highest clock and power-saving profile; NVIDIA's highest clock, power limit where it can be given one (not on a laptop) and persistence. Applied through polkit, kept for the computer and set again at every start. A sleeping NVIDIA GPU isn't asked (that would wake it): what it said last is shown.

title: Display: Colour, with HDR
caption: Preferences ▸ Display has a Colour tab beside the panel's facts: what the display shows (its gamut and light, from its EDID), whether sRGB's colours are shown accurately (converted into a wide display's gamut, the default) or vivid, and HDR on a display that takes it, with everything else's brightness and a band that reverts HDR unless kept. On a headless screen pretending to be a P3 HDR panel.

title: Olo Rescue
caption: Ctrl+Shift+Super+Delete, from anywhere: every window put away, the displays, keyboard and pointer on safe settings, and a screen of its own with a terminal (its own, in process), the processes to end, Preferences' panels (what's changed applies as Rescue ends), the displays' settings reset, Start Over, Log Out, Restart and Leave Rescue.

title: Backup chooses what goes in
caption: Preferences ▸ Backup: a check box for each part of a backup (each app's settings with the passwords and sign-ins that go with them, and the Wi-Fi networks), exporting and importing: a backup of everything can bring back the Token Pool alone. The rest stays as it is.

title: Olo Suggestions: just, uv, mise and worktrunk
caption: Programs worth having, suggested while they're not installed: just and uv from Fedora's repositories, mise and worktrunk from their makers' GitHub releases (SHA-256 checked, native); and worktrunk set to make worktrees where Terminal does.

title: A notification for each new suggestion, once
caption: Olo Suggestions tells of a suggestion once ever; at 1×, 1.5× and 2×. Its action used to be cut off past the banner's edge: banner actions now fit, stacked when they must.

title: Banner actions stack when they don't fit side by side
caption: Two long actions, one above another at the card's width, at 1×, 1.5× and 2×; a label cut with … only when even a row of its own is too narrow.

title: Agent Screens: a stopped screen stays, with Start Screen
caption: Stopping a screen keeps it, listed under Stopped (even one no agent acted on, which used to vanish), with Start Screen to start it again at its size; archived screens under Archived, shown by default. The same from olo-screen: list (with each screen's state), start NAME, archive, unarchive, delete.

title: Preferences ▸ Keyboard knows the Magic Keyboard with Touch ID
caption: The A2520 recognised by its name, in a box of its own with a picture (the keyboard icon for now), what it is, and why its Touch ID isn't used: its sensor is sealed to the Mac it's paired with.

title: A screen recording, played back in the Viewer
caption: olo-screenshot --record made it (frames only as the screen changed, H.264 into an MP4 written as it goes); Agent Screens record theirs with olo-screen record-video, at 4K too.

title: Screen recording from a shortcut: Deskbar's record light, then the notification
caption: Shift-Cmd-6 records the screen; Deskbar's tray shows a red record light with Stop Recording while it goes; finished, a notification says it was saved, with Show in Tracker.

title: Preferences ▸ GPUs: what screen recordings encode on
caption: The most powerful there is by default (here the NVIDIA RTX PRO 2000's encoder, NVENC), that GPU, or the processor (OpenH264); the recorder reads it unless told.

title: Deskbar: a paused recording
caption: A recording paused (olo-screenshot --pause, or Pause Recording in this menu) shows a pause sign in its record light's ring: two bars on device pixels, as far apart as they are wide, centred at 1x, 1.5x and 2x. Top: paused, light, 2x. Below: paused and recording, dark, 2x. The menu offers Resume Recording for Pause Recording; the pause is cut out of the video.

title: Screenshot: Record…
caption: Screenshot's window records too: Record… offers Record Screen, Record Active Window (the one behind it) and Record Region… (dragged out on the frozen screen). Its window steps aside, the recorder starts on its own and Screenshot quits; with a recording going, the menu is Pause (or Resume) and Stop Recording. The window is as tall as its form now: a fixed height had let Save in: slip under the buttons. Dark, 2x.

title: Preferences > GPUs: the power mode sets them all
caption: The power mode is the computer's one setting for speed against battery: Power Saver puts every GPU on Cooler and Quieter, Balanced on Balanced, Performance on Fastest, as it sets the processors, wherever it's chosen (a root service, olo-gpu-follow, installed by the first Apply). Its box says so and the mode now; Apply and Revert end the tuning's section, and Screen Recordings starts a section down (the layout review's new after-commit check found it 15 pt under Apply). Dark, 2x.

title: Window menu: a dialog floats always
caption: An alert or a dialog that names its window floats over it whatever is asked: in auto-tiling its window menu shows Float Over the Tiles checked and dimmed, and app_server leaves it floating when asked to tile it (an alert tiled by hand had stayed over its app's floating windows as their child: a tile over floats, found by the auto fuzzer).

title: HDR video shown for an sRGB screen
caption: HDR10 and HLG video (phones', streaming's: BT.2020, PQ or HLG) converted for an ordinary screen: its light counted in SDR's white (203 cd/m²), BT.2020 converted to sRGB, highlights rolled off up to the brightest it was mastered to. A test pattern, a PQ ramp to 1,000 cd/m² over BT.2020 colour bars at 100 and 600 cd/m²: above as it shows now, below as before (dull and grey, its samples taken as sRGB).

title: Preferences ▸ Themes: Cube, Platinum and Workbench
caption: Three more themes, after NeXTSTEP, Mac OS 9 and AmigaOS: a full icon set each (135, drawn by gpt-image-2.5-sunburst against each theme's references), its wordmark, its wallpaper (light and dark) and its own colours. The panel lays the chosen theme's colour sets beside the ten rows, so it fits 1280 × 800 without scrolling.

title: Workbench, dark: deep blue and orange
caption: The Workbench theme's dark colours (Workbench 1.3's blue, orange tab and selection, black outlines), its pixel-art icons and wallpaper.

title: Platinum, light
caption: The Platinum theme: platinum grey, a lavender tab, lilac-blue selection, its outlined icons and wallpaper.

title: Cube, light
caption: The Cube theme: workstation greys, a black tab, deep blue selection, its airbrushed icons and studio wallpaper.

title: Preferences ▸ Security: Security Keys
caption: A security key (a YubiKey) set up so a touch of it stands for the account password: the password checked, then two touches; a spare the same way; and three touches in a row to type its code where you are. Shown set up with the test key.

title: Terminal's sudo window: touch your security key
caption: With a key set up and plugged in, the window says a touch will do; the password the key keeps goes to sudo's prompt.

title: The lock screen: touch your security key
caption: Asked as the screen locks, again three times, then whenever someone is there.

title: Clicks and shortcuts shown while recording
caption: Record… ▸ Show Clicks and Show Shortcuts (or --show-clicks, --show-keys): a ring spreads where a button is pressed, and a shortcut shows on a key cap low on the screen, written as the keyboard profile writes it; typing never shows. Drawn by app_server, so recordings, screen sharing and agents' demos have them.

title: The Viewer's Trim…
caption: Edit ▸ Trim… on a video puts a handle at each end of its timeline (what's cut dimmed, the picture where a handle is dragged shown); Trim copies the stretch kept into “NAME (trimmed).mp4” beside it, nothing encoded again, and shows it. olo-screenshot --trim does the same for agents.

title: A window recorded on a background
caption: Record… ▸ Window on a Background (or --background): a window's recording shows it on the wallpaper, blurred and a little dimmed, its corners rounded and a soft shadow under it, as a polished demo of one app usually looks. Made once as the recording starts; each frame copies only the window.

title: The pointer in a recording, larger and smoothed
caption: Record… ▸ Larger Pointer and Smooth Pointer (or --pointer-size, --smooth-pointer): recordings draw the pointer bigger (drawn at that size, never enlarged) and gliding after the real one, so a hand's jitter is smoothed and an agent's jumps become moves. Here, the frames after one jump laid over each other, a thirtieth of a second apart. Only recordings have it; a window's recording now shows the pointer too.

title: Recordings zoom in on clicks
caption: Record… ▸ Zoom on Clicks (or --zoom-follow): a recording of the screen glides in around each click (twice), pans to keep the pointer in view, holds while you click and type, and glides out three seconds after; a shortcut's key cap stays in its place, unzoomed. Agents zoom to a detail themselves (olo-screen zoom-video NAME X,Y,W,H, then out). The GPU draws the capture magnified, so it costs the recorder nothing; screenshots and the screen are as they are.

title: The camera in a bubble while recording
caption: Record… ▸ Show Camera (or --camera): the camera in a circle low in the screen's right corner while you record, so a recording of the screen has you in it; it's there before the countdown, so you can frame yourself, and drags anywhere. The camera is read natively (V4L2, in process); here a stand-in camera's pattern.

title: Recordings in HEVC, and a third smaller in H.264
caption: Preferences ▸ GPUs ▸ Format: H.264 (plays everywhere) or HEVC (about half the size), on NVIDIA's encoder; olo-screenshot --codec takes AV1 too. Each codec now keeps a constant, measured quality instead of a bitrate: the same screen typed into for 5 s was 262 KB in H.264 and is 171 now, 96 in HEVC, the text as sharp. Trimming, GIFs and the Viewer take all three.

title: Captions and chapters in recordings
caption: An agent narrating a demo puts captions in the video (olo-screen caption-video: drawn into the recording only, never on the screen) and marks its steps (mark-video): the marks become the video's chapters, which the Viewer shows as ticks on its timeline and lists in Go, playing from the one chosen.

title: Display: keep HDR or a new resolution in an alert
caption: Turning HDR on (or choosing a resolution) in Preferences ▸ Display now asks in an alert over the window, counting down, Revert or Keep (the default), as BeOS's Screen preferences did; the line at the foot of the window was easy to miss, and HDR went off by itself 15 s later (Ben, 2026-11-05). The kit's widgets::open_timed_alert.

title: Display: Everything else's brightness up to 600 cd/m², on its track
caption: The SDR-in-HDR slider went to 480 while app_server took 600 (and a built-in panel's now follows its brightness, near 600 on the ThinkPad's OLED), so its knob was drawn past the track's end (Ben: it 'runs off the side'). One range for both, in protocol; the kit's Slider draws a value outside its range at the end; the note under it level with the label. At 2×, 1.5× and 1×.

title: Backgrounds: the pack's pictures have HDR versions
caption: On a display in HDR the chosen pack picture shows in HDR, its lights above everything else's white (a gain map beside each picture, made from it); Backgrounds says so under the pictures.

title: HDR wallpapers: what shines (tinted red)
caption: The gain maps wallpaper-hdr made, shown as a red tint where each picture goes above SDR's white in HDR: the sun's glow and LEDs, the moon, glints, the neon grid, speculars; the large blue and yellow surfaces and the skies stay at SDR's white.

title: Olo Doctor: temporary files on disk
caption: Doctor finds programs keeping their temporary files in memory (/tmp a tmpfs, TMPDIR unset) and offers to keep them in /var/tmp: an environment.d file of Olo's and the running session's environment.

title: Passwords is the SSH agent
caption: Preferences ▸ Security ▸ Be the SSH agent (on by default): ssh and git sign in with the SSH keys in Passwords, each terminal allowed the first time; where ~/.ssh/config sends ssh to another agent (1Password's app's), it says so and offers the switch once the session has Passwords' agent.

title: Deskbar: Ethernet beside Wi-Fi, with each link's details
caption: An Ethernet port shows in the tray while a wired link is connected. With both connected, the link not carrying the traffic (NetworkManager's default route) is drawn faint. A right-click on either shows what it's joined to, whether it's in use, its signal and rate or speed, addresses, router, DNS servers, interface, hardware address and traffic, then Network Preferences…. Here Wi-Fi stands by while Ethernet carries the traffic (nm-fake, a stand-in NetworkManager).

title: Preferences ▸ Network: Service Order, with Deskbar following
caption: Network has tabs for Ethernet, Service Order, DNS, Hosts and Shaping now. Here Wi-Fi was put first. NetworkManager's per-kind route metrics, written as root by olo-net-admin, moved the default route without disconnecting anything, and Deskbar's tray drew Ethernet faint and Wi-Fi strong as it happened (nm-fake standing in for NetworkManager).

title: Preferences ▸ Network ▸ Shaping, as a link conditioner
caption: A link made slower, later and lossier than it is, each way, to try a program on a poor network: bandwidth, delay, jitter and loss, from a network to start from (Edge, 3G, LTE, DSL, Busy Wi-Fi, Very Bad Network, Offline). The kernel's netem does it, spoken to over rtnetlink by olo-net-admin as root (an ifb device carries what's received). Here 3G was chosen and is ready to turn on.

title: Preferences ▸ Network ▸ VPN, with WireGuard imported natively
caption: The VPNs saved (WireGuard, and NetworkManager's plugins' OpenVPN, IPsec…) are each connected and disconnected here, and removed after asking. A WireGuard file (wg-quick's .conf) is imported natively: keys checked, addresses by family, and its DNS asked alone while it's up so a full tunnel's names don't leak. Here “Office” was imported and connected. Also new: a hotspot under Wi-Fi, and IPv6 and MTU on a wired link (nm-fake standing in for NetworkManager).

title: Viewer: a PDF's text selected, copied and found
caption: A PDF's text is read natively (hayro's interpreter with a device of Olo's own that keeps each glyph's Unicode and box), once a page, on the worker. It's selected by dragging (a word with a double-click, a line with a triple), copied with ⌘C or a right-click, Select All copies the whole document, and Find (⌘F) marks every match, selecting the one shown in the middle of the view. Here the third of 90 'compression's in bzip2's manual, the next one marked.

title: Viewer: text and formatted documents selected, copied and found
caption: Texts and formatted documents (Markdown, Word, OpenDocument) select as anywhere in Olo: a drag, a word with a double-click, a line with a triple, drawn behind the text in the kit's selection. Copy and Select All are in the Edit menu, and Find uses the kit's find bar, the same as PDFs': every match marked, even in a code block, with the one shown selected. Here Olo's README, looking for 'olo'.

title: Preferences ▸ Security: Face Unlock
caption: A look at the infrared camera can stand for the password: sudo, administrator requests, Passwords and the lock screen. Olo reads the IR camera over V4L2, lights its emitter through its UVC control, finds and recognises faces with two small models in process, and keeps the faces with a root service no app can read. Install… sets it up as root through Olo's polkit agent; Set Up… takes the password and five looks.

title: Agent Screens: Move Windows To…
caption: Beside Take Control, every window on the screen goes to one of the person's display-workspaces, its program running on (Control ▸ Move Windows To ▸ too).

title: Window menu: Move to Agent Screen
caption: A window's tab menu puts the window on an agent screen (or a new one), the program running on: an Olo app re-executed there, any other program replayed there by olo-wlproxy.

title: Terminal: a tab to an agent screen
caption: Terminal's tab menu sends one tab to an agent screen: a Terminal there takes its shell, which keeps running in the person's olo-termd.

title: A Terminal window moved to an agent screen
caption: The same shell (its pid) on the screen, typed into there.

title: Private windows kept out of shares
caption: Left: the screen as the person sees it (and a screenshot). Right: the same moment as a screen share or recording gets it, Passwords blacked out; the polkit prompt, Terminal's sudo prompt and the lock screen likewise.

title: A shared window, ringed
caption: While an app shares a window, it has a red ring round its body on screen (never in what's shared), flush outside its border at every scale.

title: A window's recording with the camera
caption: Recording a window on a background with Show Camera: the camera (here the stand-in's pattern) drawn on the background's corner, ringed as the on-screen bubble is.

title: Upgrading Olo: the veil
caption: While a restarted app_server brings the windows back, every display shows Olo's wordmark and a row of icons lit stage by stage, after BeOS's boot screen; it lifts once the windows are back.

title: Starting Olo: the start-up screen
caption: As a session starts, every display shows Olo's start-up screen (the upgrade veil's look, its own icons), lit as the displays, the desktop and Deskbar come up; Olo's start-up sound plays once a session.

title: olo-slack: Slack as an Olo app
caption: Slack's web app in Olo's Chrome on a profile of its own; its window is olo.slack, so Deskbar names it Slack with Olo's icon.

title: olo-slack: Slack's notifications are Olo's
caption: A Slack message as an Olo notification (Message style, Slack's edge); a click goes to the conversation. Shown here from a stand-in page.

title: Palm trainer on the ThinkPad: a palm drawn as one
caption: The ThinkPad's pad gives no contact size (its pressure is the click's force: a resting palm weighs 0), so palms were drawn as dots. Now a palm the touchpad marks is drawn palm-sized and a fingertip fingertip-sized; the trainer runs the ThinkPad's own model.

title: Preferences ▸ Touchpad on a ThinkPad: its own palm model
caption: On the ThinkPad's pad: palms kept palms until they lift, Olo's own model for this kind of touchpad (made from Ben's hands), and no pressure controls it has no use for.

title: Quick Look scrolls without the pointer moving first
caption: Space in Tracker opened Quick Look under a still pointer, and a touchpad scroll went nowhere until the pointer moved: Smithay only looks at what's under the pointer when it moves. app_server now enters what is under the pointer before a scroll or a click, and as a window comes on screen, forward or away; GPUI takes the place it's entered at as a move, so the cursor and hover are right at once. Here Quick Look, scrolled by the touchpad straight after Space.

title: Remote control: the picker asks to share and control
caption: The RemoteDesktop portal: a program that wants to see a screen and control the keyboard and pointer (Chrome Remote Desktop, Deskflow, a call's remote control) gets the screen picker, titled Share and Control Your Screen, saying what it will control, its button Allow. For control alone, the permission dialog asks. Never remembered: asked every time.

title: Remote control in Deskbar, with Stop Remote Control
caption: While a program controls the computer, Deskbar's sharing item says so (An app is controlling your keyboard and pointer) and Stop Remote Control ends the session: app_server closes its libei connection and lets go of keys left down.

title: Screen recordings on the Intel GPU: AV1 through VA-API
caption: Preferences ▸ GPUs ▸ Screen Recordings offers the Intel GPU where its VA-API driver encodes AV1 (Fedora's drivers make no H.264 or HEVC): recordings are AV1 at constant quality, a 2560 × 1600 screen in about 9 ms a frame, the NVIDIA GPU left asleep.

title: Terminal: Keep It Going for a coding agent that stopped
caption: On a tab with Claude Code or Codex, its menu has Keep It Going: after two minutes with nothing at all changing on its screen (Codex's goal clock doesn't count) and its turn over, Terminal says "please continue" to it, at most once an hour. The tab's icon carries a blue disc with a go-on triangle while it's on.

title: StyledEdit: Markdown as it looks
caption: A .md file opens as a Markdown document edited as it looks (Typora's way): headings, emphasis, inline code on its ground, links, bullets, numbers and task boxes hanging in their indents, a quotation's bar, a code block coloured by its fence's language, front matter; the marks that make them hidden off the caret's line.

title: StyledEdit: Markdown's marks show on the caret's line
caption: On the line being edited, the marks show dimmed, as typed (*emphasis*, **strong**, ~~struck~~, backticks, [link](address)); elsewhere they're hidden.

title: StyledEdit: Markdown's source, ⌘/
caption: Document ▸ Show Source (⌘/) shows the same text as a code editor: the monospaced face, line numbers, headings, links, code and marks coloured; the caret and view kept across the switch.

title: StyledEdit: source code coloured by syntax
caption: A source file (by its name, extension or #! line) opens in the kit's code view: tree-sitter grammars for 43 languages, parsed on a worker, colours from the palette (dark mode here), line numbers in a gutter.

title: StyledEdit: Markdown tables as grids
caption: A Markdown table shows as a ruled grid (the editor's table rows, its cells the text between the pipes, columns as wide as their longest cell, the header shaded, the |---| line hidden off the caret), typed in cell by cell: Tab to the next, Return adds a row.

title: StyledEdit: Markdown pictures
caption: ![alt](file) shows as the picture it names (a file beside the document), off the caret's line.

title: StyledEdit: Markdown table columns aligned
caption: A Markdown table's columns align as its delimiter row says (:--- left, :---: centre, ---: right): the editor's rows take each column's own alignment (Row::aligns).

title: Viewer: a video at Actual Size, Zoom to Fit and Zoom to Fill
caption: View ▸ Actual Size (⌘0), Zoom to Fit (⌘9), Zoom to Fill (⇧⌘9), proportions kept; Enter Full Screen (F), the transport over the picture while the pointer moves

title: Touchpad & Mouse: the wheel's scrolling speed
caption: One speed for a wheel's notch in every program, Chrome included (app_server scales it before it's sent); at 1.5×

title: Olo Setup: Welcome, full screen on a stock Fedora 45
caption: Windows 95's Setup in BeOS's look: the blue backdrop and big serif title, a BeOS window for each page. Downloaded and run in a fresh Fedora 45 Workstation VM, 1x.

title: Olo's login screen after Setup, on a fresh Fedora 45
caption: Restarted from Setup's last page: Olo's own login screen in GDM's place, Olo Desktop chosen.

title: Olo on a fresh Fedora 45, installed by Setup
caption: Logged in through Olo's login screen; Home open in Tracker and Preferences switched to dark.

title: Power ▸ Graphics says what each GPU is on now
caption: Ben asked whether changing the power mode changes the NVIDIA GPU's clock. It does in Power Saver (its clock capped at 70%), but its box showed only its Custom slider, at the card's top clock whatever the mode, while Intel's sliders moved: now each GPU's line says what the mode has it on, in numbers (here Performance: Intel 1650–2450 MHz; NVIDIA as its driver has it, since a laptop's takes no power limit), and Custom's sliders show Custom's own settings, which don't move with the mode.

title: Olo Doctor: ignored findings, quietly last
caption: Every finding has Ignore beside its fix. What's ignored leaves the count, Fix All, the tray's bag and the notifications, and is listed last under Ignored, dim, with Stop Ignoring and its fix should the person change their mind. Doctor also offers Olo's own login screen where another's greets (not shown here: the sandbox's build has no olo-login).

title: Deskbar: live widgets
caption: Deskbar's new live widgets, as BeOS's Pulse and ProcessController put bars in its tray: a temperature and a CPU graph in the tray; under it a CPU graph, each core's bars, a memory-and-swap meter and the network's down and up; at the foot, the GPU and the system volume. Each is read on a worker only while shown, as often as it asks.

title: Preferences ▸ Deskbar
caption: The new Deskbar panel: the widgets in order (Add, Remove, Move Up, Move Down) beside the chosen one's settings: what it shows and which, where, look, size, name and value, how often, how far back, colour. Each change shows in the Deskbar at once.

title: DiskBackup: Keep, and tidying
caption: How long snapshots are kept (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly), beside When; Speed moved beside Back Up To so the window still fits 1280 × 800. The status says what the backups take there and the last tidy (old snapshots let go of, space freed).

title: DiskBackup in Deskbar's tray
caption: A drive in a circular arrow: idle, backing up (green), not backing up (dim: off, on battery), the last didn't finish (red dot), nothing for days (amber). Its menu, read as it opens: what it's doing, the last and next, Stop or Back Up Now, Pause, Restore Files…, DiskBackup…. Light and dark at 2×.

title: Tracker: DiskBackup's ticks and Older Versions
caption: Files whose current version is backed up wear a green tick, in every view and on the desktop (a changed file loses it until the next backup). A file's Older Versions… opens DiskBackup's Versions window: each version kept, the one there now said; Restore keeps both or replaces.

title: DiskBackup's own icon, in every theme
caption: A hard drive with a cloud before it, a green tick on the cloud (backed up, safe elsewhere), in place of Preferences ▸ Backup's drive and arrow (top row of each band: DiskBackup; under it, Backup's), at 64 and 16 px on the light, dark and night panels.

title: Tracker's list view: one edge at its foot
caption: The count bar under the list view no longer draws its etched edge: the list's own sunken frame (its focus ring inside) edges it, and the two had stacked four lines in three points (tsession review: crowded lines, at 1× and 2×). Light and dark, 2× and 1×.

title: DiskBackup: Back Up to Google Drive, walked through
caption: Google asks each person to make their own sign-in for an app like DiskBackup, so DiskBackup walks them through it: six steps in Google Cloud, each with Open for its page, then the client's file (or its ID and secret) and Sign In with Google. A client kept in Passwords skips the steps on another computer.

title: Disk Usage: Undo Move to Trash
caption: Edit ▸ Undo puts what Disk Usage moved to the Trash back where it was (its sizes back in the chart); Redo moves it again. Deleting for good still says it can't be undone.

title: DiskBackup: Edit ▸ Undo for its settings
caption: Each settings change in DiskBackup's window is a step named for what it changed (Leave Out, Keep, Speed, Patterns typed as one run); Undo puts back only that, leaving what the service or a setup changed since.

title: Notifications: Undo Clear All and Forget
caption: The History window's Edit ▸ Undo brings back what Clear All or Forget took, where it was (closed at its app by now); Redo forgets it again.

title: Security Keys: a key with a PIN
caption: A security key with a PIN set is set up with it (asked once, not kept): the key's PIN beside the account password, a wrong one said with the tries left. Its Remove works beside Face Unlock's (the two Remove buttons had one id and lost their clicks).

title: Every app clean at 1.25× and 1.75×
caption: The layout review at 1.25× and 1.75× had found 26 errors and 10 near-misses across the apps, all there before: Power's grid (here, even now), boxes' insets, right-aligned labels, text fields in rows, Screen Saver's monitor stand, Telegram's panes, check boxes beside menus, Network's columns, About's wordmark. Every app and panel is clean at 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 and 2×.

title: Always on Top, from a window's menu
caption: A window's tab menu has Always on Top: kept above the others (its dialogs over it still, picture in picture over it), across a reload; agents set it with set_on_top.

title: The overview: windows dragged between workspaces, and New Workspace
caption: In the overview (⌃Space) a window dragged onto another workspace's pane goes there, and onto New Workspace (the strip at the side) to an empty one, made if every one has windows; the overview stays out and lays itself out again. A click on New Workspace shows an empty one.

title: Passwords: a terminal's op or ssh allowed with a touch or a look
caption: The Allow alert for a terminal session's op, or its first SSH signature, now says what else allows it (Touch ID, a security key set up, face unlock) and waits for it while open: a touch here took it away and op went on. Shown at 2× with a test's soft key.

title: Telegram: voice messages recorded
caption: Nothing to send, Telegram's send button is a microphone: hold it and speak (the time and live levels in the field), let go on it to send, away from it to cancel; a click records until Send, × or Escape. Opus in Ogg, coded in process (rusty-opus, kept to SILK). Shown at 2× with a test's fake microphone.

title: Telegram: animated stickers play
caption: Lottie stickers (Telegram's .tgs) now play: once as they come into view, and again while the pointer is over them, each frame drawn at the sticker's own device size on a worker (velato, vendored with its panics on real files fixed, drawn by vello_cpu). The demo's is Olo's own beating heart, caught mid-beat with its ring.

title: Auto-tiling: Main and Stack, and a layout picker
caption: Auto-tiling has a second layout, Main and Stack (as dwm's): a new window is the main one on the left, the others stack on the right, each as tall. Chosen from Deskbar's windowing mode menu (Auto-Tiling Layout) or Preferences ▸ Windows. Every tile changing size now lands in the same frame (one round).

title: Olo Setup: Choose What to Install
caption: On a fresh Fedora 45 in a VM, Olo's login screen and boot splash chosen. Retaken: the 2026-11-07 picture of this page had only its top left corner (a 1× shot cropped as if 2×).

title: Olo Setup: Installing
caption: Step 3 of 8: the release downloaded (947 MB) and checked; the stages so far below. Retaken, as above.

title: Olo Setup: Olo Is Installed
caption: Olo 2026.11.08-66af29d4 installed. Retaken, as above.

title: Olo's login screen after Setup, its steps now shared with Doctor
caption: After the restart: the login-screen stage Setup and Olo Doctor share since 3a040276 (olo_doctor::login_screen), tried on a stock Fedora for the first time since that move.

title: Olo after Setup on a fresh Fedora, in use
caption: Tracker on Home, StyledEdit, Olo Doctor (two suggestions, no other desktop's daemons) and Preferences switched to dark.

title: Olo's boot splash on a Fedora 45 that Olo Setup set up
caption: In the installer check's VM, booting as a stock install does (rhgb quiet): Plymouth shows Olo's theme, the wordmark, the four icons and Starting Olo…. Not seen in that VM before: its text install had left the serial console and no rhgb.

title: Where Olo's login screen can't show, GDM's takes the seat
caption: A GPU Olo can't draw on (the VM's plain virtio GPU): after Olo's splash, GDM's login screen, started by systemd through olo-login's OnFailure=. Before, SELinux kept olo-login from starting it and the screen stayed on the console.

title: Keyboard ▸ Power Button
caption: Preferences ▸ Keyboard has a Power Button tab: what the computer's own power button does when pressed, and when held for a number of seconds, each from Nothing, Lock the Screen, Log Out, Restart (asking first, or not, or immediately) and Shut Down (the same three). By default a press does nothing, holding it 3 seconds asks to restart (Deskbar's Restart alert), and 10 seconds shuts down at once. Immediately needs Olo's small helper, which Install the Helper… (Olo Doctor's fix) puts in place. It is a tab of its own because the Keyboard tab with it no longer fit a 1280 × 800 screen.

title: Every way in at once: the finger and the password
caption: An administrator request (polkit) with Touch ID set up: the password, or a security key's touch, is taken while the fingerprint sensor listens, not after it gives up. Once polkit's PAM listens for a finger, a second conversation asks for the password; the first to succeed counts. sudo's window in Terminal does the same. Setting up Touch ID had made Ben's YubiKey wait behind the fingerprint.

title: Security ▸ Sign In: Touch ID, Face Unlock and Security Keys together
caption: Preferences ▸ Security has two tabs. Sign In has every way in besides the password, each standing for it wherever it's asked, all at once. Touch ID, which was a panel of its own, is a box beside Face Unlock and Security Keys. The Passwords tab has Passwords' and programs' secrets settings. The old names (touchid, fingerprint, passwords) open the right tab.

title: Deskbar: Group All Windows, as the windows are
caption: Deskbar's menu for an app says what its windows are, not a setting: Group All Windows when they aren't all in one group (here one was taken out by hand), Ungroup All Windows when they are. Group All puts every one back in; Ungroup All takes each out in a cascade, every tab showing. Before, Group Windows was ticked whenever the app's grouping was on, even with windows out of the group.

title: Night Mode: shift gradually
caption: Preferences ▸ Appearance ▸ Night Mode can warm gradually: scheduled, it shifts from neutral to its warmth over 1 minute to 3 hours from its start, in steps too small to see, and is back to neutral at its end as before (no shift out).

title: Move to Window, for every tab
caption: A tab's menu, and a tab group's, has Move to Window ▸ with the app's other windows by title: the kit's Menu::move_to_window. Terminal's tabs and tab groups move there (a group stays a group), and the window they leave closes if nothing's left; a window's own tab (here StyledEdit's) joins the other window's group.

title: DiskBackup: Agent Setup
caption: Back Up to Google Drive ▸ Let an Agent Do It…: choose the Google account's login from Passwords; DiskBackup starts an agent screen, shares the login with it, and opens Claude Code in a Terminal window to make Google's sign-in for DiskBackup there, then hand it back (olo-diskbackup --agent-setup-done), with the consent page allowed on the agent's screen. Tried for real: the agent did the steps in 9 minutes.

title: Preferences ▸ AI: Claude Code's model
caption: The model and thinking Olo starts Claude Code with for a task (DiskBackup's Agent Setup): Opus 5.5 on Medium by default.

title: DiskBackup, redesigned: what it's doing now, its plan, every setting
caption: Ben asked for an intuitive, full-featured backup app. A header says whether your files are safe; while a backup runs, the file it's at, a bar of bytes against the plan, files, time left, what's new and sent against the upload limit. Five tabs: Schedule (automatic or only when you click Back Up Now; what's kept, said plainly), Files, Backups, Speed & Resources (upload and download limits; the priority: idle, gently or full speed), Destination. Fits 1280×800 while backing up.

title: DiskBackup's Backups tab: every snapshot, delete some or erase all
caption: Choose one or several backups and delete them (asked first; the space only they took is freed at once), or Erase All Backups to start fresh.

title: DiskBackup: unfinished backups, and each one validated
caption: A backup that's stopped keeps what it got through and the next goes on from it (listed first, Unfinished, deletable to free what it sent). Each backup is validated fast once it's made (checksums compared with the store's, a sample read back); Validate does that for any, Validate Fully reads every byte back.

title: DiskBackup's Destination: what it's connected to, and Disconnect
caption: Whose Google Drive, its folder, Connected, what the backups take and the Drive's space (as Google says); Disconnect…, Use a Folder Instead…, Open in Google Drive. A folder says its disk's space.

title: DiskBackup validating: what's read back, of how much
caption: Validate Fully at a 2 MB/s download limit: every pack the backups need read back and checked, as a restore would; Stop works throughout.

title: Connecting Google Drive again: the sign-in from before filled in
caption: After Disconnect, Connect Google Drive… fills in the client made before and folds the steps away (Show the Steps); with them shown the window now fits 1280 x 800 (708 points).

title: DiskBackup says what it's doing, plainly
caption: What it backs up (your home folder), how far through how much (more than the last backup's, when it is), files, time left, then what's new to the backup and what's sent, compressed and encrypted; Deskbar's menu says the same.

title: Stopping a backup, said as it goes
caption: Stopping the moment Stop is clicked (or an upgrade asks): the pack being sent finished first, how much of it and how long, then what's done is kept for the next to go on from.

title: Terminal: what Keep It Going says, yours to choose
caption: Preferences ▸ Terminal ▸ Coding Agents: Keep It Going says “Please continue” unless you change it; Use Default puts it back. Terminal follows it at once.

title: Token Pool shows every quota an account has
caption: The session (5-hour, “not started” before its first request), the week, and each model's own week (Weekly Fable, Weekly Sonnet), as Claude's usage report lists them; Codex's own limits too. Made-up accounts.

title: DiskBackup: waiting for the network
caption: No network mid-backup (a cable pulled, Wi-Fi left): the backup waits for one and says so, and goes on by itself, from where it got to, once it's back; a connection on a network that went is cut at once and the request asked again on the new one (olo-net). A sandboxed service in a network namespace of its own, its way out taken away.

title: DiskBackup's title over its buttons (before)
caption: While a backup started, its title ("Getting ready: counting what to back up", or a folder named by its path) ran on over Restore… and Stop: the layout lint didn't look at DiskBackup, and had no check for text over a control.

title: DiskBackup's title fits beside its buttons
caption: Shorter titles ("Counting what to back up", "Backup didn't finish"), and a folder's path cut short with its whole in the tip. The layout review now finds text that runs over a control (text-over-control), and the lint draws DiskBackup's window in all 25 of its states.

title: Telegram: a right-click on the archive acts on all its chats
caption: Mark All as Read, Mute All, Unmute All and Unarchive All… on the archive's row; folders' chips, Unknown Senders and the More chip (a submenu each) have the same; Chat ▸ Mark All as Read for the list shown. Demo account.

title: Telegram: folders behind More, a submenu each
caption: A right-click on the More chip: each folder behind it with Mark All as Read, Mute All, Unmute All. Demo account.

title: Terminal: Auto Approve counts down to Yes
caption: A coding agent's "Do you want to proceed?" (here a stand-in drawing Claude Code's dialog) answered Yes after 30 s (6 s in this test), unless the person types in the tab or presses Stop; the countdown in the pane's corner.

title: Terminal: Auto Approve in a tab's menu
caption: Beside Keep It Going (and in Tabs). Turned on from the commands socket (an agent, the palette), it asks the person first.

title: Window tab menu: Close Others in a group
caption: A window in a group: Close Others after Close closes every other window of its group, each as its close box would (one with unsaved work asks).

title: AppImages show their own icons everywhere
caption: An AppImage's icon, read out of its image, now shows for its file in Tracker (with or without the .AppImage extension), for its running windows in Deskbar and the Twitcher, and under its own name in the window menu. Each AppImage known gets a hidden desktop entry, so every app lookup finds it; one run from a folder nothing looked at is found by its process (here DBDelve, run from a folder of its own).

title: Videos and sounds play at 0.25× to 2×
caption: Quick Look and the Viewer have a speed button at the transport's right end: it says the speed and opens the speeds over itself, 0.25× to 2×; > and < step faster and slower, and the Viewer's View menu has them too. The sound keeps its pitch (time-stretched, as SoundTouch does it) and the picture follows it.

title: Terminal: each agent's own Keep It Going message
