caption: Keep It Going is a submenu in a tab's menu: on or off, the default message, or one of the tab's own (Custom Message…), kept with the tab. Keep It Going and Auto Approve now work with the real Claude Code and Codex: Codex's reasoned questions are answered, Claude Code's blinking marker no longer delays the answer, and nothing is typed into a chooser.

title: Olo Doctor finds Token Pool running twice
caption: A Token Pool started beside the one serving, unable to take its port, served nothing for two days while its window showed no requests. Olo Doctor now finds it and quits it; the session starts it again, and it keeps the one serving rather than running beside it.

title: Screenshot: New screenshot shows the new picture
caption: Screenshot moved to Olo's own kit. Its preview was kept while the picture's size was the same, so New screenshot went on showing the one before; a preview is now of one picture. The region and colour pickers show the screen a pixel to a device pixel at 1.5× and 1.75× too (the overlay's whole-point size was half a device pixel off the screen's, and the frozen picture was stretched by it).

title: Activity Monitor: the fans against what they cool
caption: Sensors has a Fans card in place of a small graph a fan: each fan's speed, the processor's temperature and how often it was throttled for heat on one graph (each to its own scale, the fans to one), the fan profile in use and the level Olo's fan service holds, and the throttling counted since the computer started and since the window opened, so a fan curve can be seen to work. (Activity Monitor is on olo-kit as of today.)

title: Passwords on olo-kit
caption: Passwords moved from GPUI to Olo's own kits: its state is the app's, behind a lock, since it runs with no window as the SSH agent and the keychain; the main window, Review Sync, Sync Problems, the generator and a passkey's question are views that read it. The same to the pixel as before at 1×, 1.5× and 2×, light and dark, but for what was wrong: the item pane's scroll bar is there as an item opens (it came with the first scroll), Sync Problems' icons are level with their items at 1×, and “Synced a minute ago” counts the minutes by itself. A frame typing in the editor went from 1.9 ms to 0.3, the arrows down a list of 508 from 1.8 to 0.8.

title: Terminal on olo-kit
caption: Terminal on Olo's own kit: one Terminal behind a lock, each window a view on a looper of its own, its screens a view of their own drawn once a frame however much a shell prints. The same to the pixel as before at every scale, light and dark; a frame of typing 475 to 240 µs, of steady output 532 to 305 µs.

title: Preferences on olo-kit
caption: Preferences, every panel, on Olo's own kits: each panel's window a view on a looper of its own. The same to the pixel as it was but for two things meant: the launcher's cells are wider (the longest names ran into the cell beside them) and Notifications' From and to line up with the words above them. Typing in a field draws in a quarter of the time, a slider in half.

title: The Installer, at work
caption: Olo Setup redone after BeOS's Installer (Ben: "redo the installer to be reminiscent of the beos installer instead of windows 95"): one window on the BeOS desktop's blue, with Olo's mark, a box of words saying what is being done, Install from and Onto as pop-ups, More Options opening the optional parts under a latch, a status bar, and Begin, which is Stop while it works. Shown in its demo mode (a made-up computer; nothing is installed).

title: The Installer
caption: As it opens once the licence is agreed to: what will happen, where from and onto what, More Options closed, About, Quit and Begin. BeOS's Installer for Olo, in place of the Windows 95 wizard of five pages.

title: Preferences ▸ Power: the fan profile
caption: Battery & Idle has a Fans box on a ThinkPad (Ben: "have in the power prefs the option for the default auto and this new cooler/louder auto profile"): Automatic, the firmware's own curve, or Cool, Olo's olo-fans running the fans ahead of the heat so the processor isn't throttled, with what the fans are doing now under it. Choosing one asks Olo Doctor to set it (an administrator's password). Shown with a made-up ThinkPad in a scratch folder.

title: Preferences ▸ Performance: the scheduler
caption: A Scheduler tab (Ben: "add to olo the ability to pick a custom scheduler in preferences -> performance and the recommendation should be scx_lavd"): the kernel's own or LAVD (recommended), what each is for, and what is scheduling now as the kernel says it. Choosing one has Olo Doctor install and start it, or stop it (an administrator's password). Shown with a made-up kernel in a scratch folder.

title: Olo Doctor: the Cool fan profile that isn't in force
caption: Cool chosen and the fans' driver taking no levels (it had been told to by hand, which a restart undid): found, with the fix that tells it to at every start. Also found: the fan service stopped, and one an upgrade has left older.

title: Activity Monitor: a fan profile that isn't in force says so
caption: The Fans card said "the fan service isn't running" of a service that was running and couldn't set the fans. It reads the service's state through olo_system::fans now: not in force and why (the driver, until the next start; the service stopped), or the level held.

title: Activity Monitor: an NVIDIA card's encoder and decoder
caption: The card's video encoder and decoder are engines of their own, which its library counts apart from graphics: a screen recording encoding on it read as an idle GPU. Each is a series now (here a 4K encode: the encoder at half, graphics at a seventh), and the card, in Activity Monitor and Deskbar's widget, is as busy as its busiest engine. Intel's render and media engines the same.

title: Deskbar: a film playing on an AirPlay receiver
caption: While olo-airplay plays a film on a receiver, Deskbar's tray has a screen with a play mark on it (two bars while paused, a count when there are several). Its menu says what plays where, with Pause (or Resume) and Stop for each, and Stop All. The mark is placed in device pixels inside the screen's frame: centred at 1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, 1.75× and 2×. Tried against a receiver of the test's own, on the loopback.

title: Preferences ▸ AirPlay: pairing with a receiver
caption: A new panel: the AirPlay receivers on the network and those paired with, each with its kind and how it is; Pair… asks one to show its code and the field takes the keyboard. Check, Forget, Show Display and Stop for one paired with. Test receivers on the loopback.

title: Show on AirPlay in a window's tab menu
caption: Right-click a window's tab: Show on AirPlay ▸ lists the receivers paired with (the kit's Menu::airplay); the same is in Deskbar's app rows, Agent Screens and Deskbar's agent screens item.

title: Play On in Viewer's File menu
caption: A film in Viewer (and in Tracker's menu) has Play On ▸: the receiver fetches and plays the file itself.

title: Deskbar's tray says a screen shown on AirPlay
caption: A window shown live on a receiver: its title, the receiver, Pause and Stop, and AirPlay Preferences…

title: Show a workspace on AirPlay from its Deskbar heading
caption: A workspace heading's menu in Deskbar has Show on AirPlay ▸ (the receivers paired with, then AirPlay Settings…): that workspace is shown live on the television though its display shows another, its windows where they were left, drawing on (Olo's own workspace capture source).

title: A workspace not shown, as AirPlay gets it
caption: What a share of workspace 2 is while the display shows workspace 1 (the desktop alone): its Terminal where it was left, under Deskbar, over the desktop and the wallpaper, drawing on (a clock printing ten lines a second kept going in the frames that followed).

title: Recordings and AirPlay in H.264 on the Intel GPU
caption: Preferences ▸ Power ▸ Graphics: where the Intel GPU's driver encodes H.264 (RPM Fusion's iHD, as here), Encode on says Intel Graphics (VA-API), not "AV1 only", and offers H.264 or AV1, measured: a 2560 × 1600 screen in about 8 ms a frame as H.264, 9 as AV1, about the same size. The same encoder shows a screen on AirPlay from frames lent by app_server, never copied: 5.0% of a core for a busy 1728 × 1080 Terminal at 60 a second, where NVENC with copies took 11.9%.

title: AirPlay's sound on the television only
caption: A showing makes an output of its own (Den (AirPlay)), listed with the others while it's shown, and moves to it the sound that goes with what's shown: a window's app's, an agent screen's programs', a display's the computer's. It plays on the television and not on the speakers; back where it was when paused or stopped.

title: Preferences ▸ Performance: the pointer on a thread of its own
caption: A Pointer box on the Scheduler tab: 'Move the pointer on a thread of its own' reads libinput on a thread of app_server's own that moves the hardware cursor while the desktop is busy, so the pointer never stops or loses motion. Off until tried; takes effect at once.

title: Tracker Status: names cut, Stop always in place
caption: Fixed at 540 points and as tall as its jobs. Under the bar, the current item's name is cut short with '…' and the counts and time left show whole at the right, so a long or changing name never pushes Stop out of the window (Ben: 'it doesn't fit in the space when the names etc are changing').

title: Preferences ▸ Sound: as tall as its devices
caption: The Sound panel's height was a 466-point minimum sized for the most devices a machine shows, so with fewer (or no sound server) the window kept empty space below. Now its height is what its devices need.

title: Tracker list view: Edit Name shows its field
caption: Before (top): F2 in the list view blanked the name and showed no field, so typing went nowhere. After: the rename field sits over the Name cell, inside the column (a longer name scrolls in it); clicks in it place the caret. The kit's ColumnListView::over_cell.

title: Power Modes: the processors' top speed
caption: Preferences ▸ Power ▸ Power Modes gets a Top speed row: how fast the processors may go in each mode and on battery, Balanced 75% by default (Ben: Balanced ran too hot, Power Saver too slow). On the ThinkPad a loaded P-core now tops out at 3.6 GHz of its 4.7 in Balanced.

title: Power Modes: an SSD row
caption: Each NVMe drive gets a row in Preferences ▸ Power ▸ Power Modes: As It Is by default (untouched), or Cooler and Coolest, its own lower working power states, with their watts once the follower has read the drive (Ben: "add the ability to adjust/customize nvme power for each profile").

title: Token Pool widgets: several quotas, a heatmap coloured by use
caption: A Token Pool widget takes any of a provider's quotas (5-hour, Weekly): a heatmap cell for each account's each, green unused to red used up; its value each quota's, shortened with its short label ('Claude 5h/Wk 24% · 45%') where the column is narrow. Made-up meters in a headless session.

title: Preferences ▸ Deskbar: a Token Pool widget's quotas as check boxes
caption: Quotas: each of the provider's, checked to show (none: whichever holds each account back). For a heatmap, Colour and 'Orange, then red' are dimmed: its cells are coloured by use.

title: Token Pool widget: Quotas is a menu field of any number
caption: The Deskbar widget editor's quotas were a row of check boxes, which a real Claude account's quota names ran past Preferences' right edge. Now a MenuField::many: it says the chosen ones, cut with … to fit, and its menu checks any of them, Whichever holds each back first. The Preferences lint now draws the editor for every widget kind with the longest quota names the services use.

title: Every app's first menu: About, Keyboard Shortcuts, its settings, Close and Quit
caption: Every Olo app's bar now starts the same way, as BeOS's did: About the app, Keyboard Shortcuts (the palette's sheet, the app's keys first), then the Preferences panels that go with it ("Performance Settings…"), and ends with Close and Quit; Edit holds Undo to Find Previous in one order, View the zooms. The kit runs these items itself, and every window's review fails a bar that strays (olo_kit::app_menu).

title: A rolled-up window is its tab, closed along its bottom
caption: Rolled up, a window shows only its tab, and the tab now closes its own bottom with its outline and its bevel's shadow, where before its bottom edge was open (it was drawn to sit on the frame). Here six rolled-up windows fanned out by Tile All; windows wider than their cell no longer put their tabs over the others'.

title: Captive portals: seen, said and a click away
caption: A network that wants its sign-in page first (NetworkManager's own connectivity check finding a portal, heard in its signals: nothing polled) now shows everywhere it should. Preferences ▸ Network says “sign-in needed” beside the connection, with Open Sign-In Page and the page itself when the network names it (DHCP option 114). Deskbar shows a globe in the tray whose tip names the network and whose click opens the page, and Notifications posts one note per network with the same action. Opening the page has NetworkManager check again every 5 s until it lets traffic through, so all of it goes as soon as you've signed in. (A stand-in NetworkManager and network here.)

title: A tip goes when its item goes from under the pointer
caption: Left, before: the pointer rests on the Wi-Fi icon, but the tip still says Ethernet. The cable icon that was there went (unplugged) without hearing that the pointer left it, so its tip stayed up for good. Now anything the pointer is over hears it leave when it goes, and what takes its place hears the pointer come. Middle and right: the pointer resting on the cable, then the cable unplugged, and the tip is the globe's, which took its place.

title: Olo Doctor: one list, each finding tagged with its kind
caption: Olo Suggestions folded into Olo Doctor (Ben: one app, each item showing whether it's a suggestion or something critical, any of it ignorable), and the window tidied: a card per finding, most pressing first, its kind's tag (Critical, Problem, Recommended, Suggestion) level with its title, Ignore as a quiet link beside its fix; the summary counts each kind; Check Again and Fix All under the list. Made-up report (OLO_DOCTOR_DEMO=1).

title: Olo Doctor in dark: what's fine under a latch
caption: Under the findings, Fixed, As It Should Be and Ignored are latches over a card of lines: As It Should Be folds away while anything is found and opens when nothing is; an applied suggestion is undone from its line (Put It Back). Ignored is folded, its tags grey.

title: Olo Doctor offers Olo's start-up screen and chime as the computer starts
caption: Two suggestions: the boot splash (Olo's Plymouth theme at the panel's scale, made into the start-up image) in place of Lenovo's and Fedora's logos, and the chime played from the built-in speakers as the computer starts, as a Mac's (olo-chime, a root service before PipeWire). Each with its way back. Doctor's made-up demo report, 2×.

title: Tracker: a band in a scrolled icon view is drawn where it is
caption: Before (left): in an icon view scrolled down, the selection band was drawn displaced up by the scroll (what it selected was right). After (right): drawn from the press to the pointer. Tracker's icon views, columns and Desktop now draw a row (an icon on the Desktop) again only when it changes; the band is a drawing over them, in the content's own coordinates.

title: Command palette's key hint, before
caption: The "Ctrl Files" hint centred by its own capitals sat ~3 pt off the 20-pt query's baseline: the layout review's near-level at 1x, 1.5x and 2x.

title: Command palette's key hint, after
caption: KeyHint::level_with(QUERY_SIZE): the hint on the query's baseline, its cap moved down with it, so the field reads as one line. The review finds nothing at 1x, 1.5x and 2x.

title: Float Window ▸ Just This Time or Always
caption: The window menu's Float Window is a submenu: this window just this time, or every window of its app always (checked here: StyledEdit floats always, and this window was tiled by hand). Unfloat of such a window asks the same.

title: Preferences ▸ Windows: apps that always float
caption: The apps floated Always, unchecked to tile them again; the panel in two columns, as one it was taller than a 1280 × 800 screen.

title: Deskbar's widget tips are cards
caption: Rest the pointer on a Deskbar widget and its tip is now a card (olo_kit::card), not a line of text: what it measures and its value at the top, the last minute as a graph, each core's bars, each series against its colour, and the processes using the most as bars; a Token Pool widget's shows each account or quota with what's left in green to red, when it resets and the one answering now. Ben: 'improve the popovers so that they can have rich widgets/designs inside of them … visually show the data better'. Light, 1×; checked at 1.5× and 2×, light and dark.

title: Folder tabs: the Labels look, in every tab strip and tab view
caption: Ben chose "folder tabs → labels". The kit's TabStrip (Terminal's tabs, along the top and down the side) draws BeOS's slanted folder tabs in Classic and Mac OS 9's rounded ones in Platinum: the chosen tab in the content's colours and open onto it, the others a shade off the panel; a group led by a label of its colour, its name in spaced bold capitals. Group colours come from the look (Palette::group_colors: Mac OS 9's Finder labels in Platinum, BeOS's bright hues in Classic; white names by day, near-black on lifted fills at night). TabView (Preferences and the rest) draws the same tabs over its raised panel; crowded, the widest are cut back and short names keep their width. Above: the tabs example in Classic light and Platinum dark at 2×.

title: Quick Look: every picture drawn, on any screen
caption: Before (top): on a 2.5× display beside a shorter one, Quick Look sized itself past the room a window that fits what it shows has; its Frame scrolled it and the picture's box was laid out to nothing, an empty body over a scroll bar after ↓. After (bottom): the Frame puts such a window back within the room each time, and Quick Look sizes itself within it.

title: Agent Screens' History back from another tab shows its rows
caption: Before (left): History, then Stats, then History again on a screen with 2,104 actions: the list blank, its scroll bar at the end, and the wheel did nothing (Ben's report). The display thread let go of the list's scroller while Stats showed and started it again at its top, while the looper had it at the end; every report after carried an old mark and was dropped. After (right): every scroll layer carries where its looper has it, and the display thread starts one it hasn't from there, so a list on any tab comes back where it was.

title: Main and Stack: the main window in any place, Center Two Thirds by default
caption: Auto-tiling's Main and Stack puts its main window in a place chosen for each display's workspace (Deskbar's Window Arrangement ▸ Main Window, any part a window tiles into; Preferences ▸ Windows for the default, Center Two Thirds), the rest stacked around it: a column either side of a main window in the middle. Make Main (⌃⌥⌘M) and Swap with Previous Main (⌃⌥⌘⌫) in the arrangement menu, the window menu, the command palette, the overview (Ctrl+letter) and keyboard hints (Ctrl held with a window's letter).

title: A menu bar too narrow for its menus keeps them under »
caption: Before (left): StyledEdit tiled at its least width, its Document menu cut off past the window's edge (the live review's error). After (right): the titles that don't fit go in a » title at the bar's end, whose menu has them as submenus, as Qt's menu bar extension and the kit toolbar's » do; agents read it as More Menus.

title: Olo Doctor fixes and applies what's checked, all, either or one kind
caption: Each finding with a fix has a check box (problems checked to begin with, suggestions when wanted); Choose: All · Problems · Suggestions · None; one default button that says what it will do (Fix 4 Problems, Apply 4 Suggestions, Fix 4 and Apply 4), as wide as its widest words so nothing moves as it counts. The kit's chosen pattern (Mac OS X's Software Update, Xcode's Update to Recommended Settings), in the Olo Book.

title: A Deskbar widget's own name
caption: Preferences ▸ Deskbar ▸ Widget has Name:, its hint what the widget is called by what it measures (CPU); the Deskbar shows the name in its row, beside others and as its card's title (CPU · over the last minute under it), a long one cut with … (Ben: "let me provide a custom name for the widget"). Dark, 1.5×.

title: The command palette: Olo's own, then files, then other apps, by Ctrl
caption: Left: ⌘Space finds Olo's own at first (its apps, commands, shortcuts, settings, windows): "term" is Olo's Terminal and its settings. Right: two taps of Ctrl later, other programs' apps only: GNOME's Terminal. The key hint says what the next tap finds (Files, Other Apps, Olo). Light, 2×.

title: Passwords makes and manages vaults
caption: File ▸ New Vault…, Vault Info… and Delete Vault… (and a vault's right-click in the sources): made, renamed, described or deleted here at once, and in 1Password at the next sync, each a row of Review Sync with the vault's icon.

title: Weather: every layer of the forecast, with an assistant
caption: A new app (apps/weather): saved places, now in six cards (cloud base and ceiling, visibility, wind, precipitation, humidity, UV), the next hour by the minute, and Rest of Today, Next 3 Days and Next 7 Days over the kit's new Timeline (temperature, clouds drawn from their base up, visibility, precipitation by kind, wind, humidity and pressure, UV; the pointer reads every layer at an hour). The assistant at the right gets the whole forecast; the spans it names are marked on the chart and listed under its answer. tomorrow.io's data for Seattle, at 2×; the answer here is a test stand-in's, not a model's.

title: Themes: two, Classic and Platinum, as cards
caption: Olo has two themes now, Classic (after BeOS) and Platinum (after Mac OS 9); the other eight and Catppuccin's colours went, and a setting naming one draws Classic. Preferences ▸ Themes shows them as two cards, each a preview of its wallpaper with a small window in its own colours and a few of its icons, its name and wordmark, a line about it and a row of its icons; its colour sets (its own and BeOS's) under them. (The wallpapers here are the old ones: new ones come next.)

title: Wallpapers: Mac OS 9's desktop pictures, made 4K
caption: The themes' wallpapers are Mac OS 9's own desktop pictures now: nineteen of the twenty it installed (all but the Finder's face), taken from a Mac OS 9 disc and made 4K with sunburst, widened to 16:9 by continuing their backgrounds. Classic's default is Blueberry Oxygen (on the desktop here), Platinum's Quantum Foam, each with a dark version. Backgrounds shows the pack one collection at a time (Collection:), its pictures in a list that scrolls.

title: Backgrounds: the retro collection, tiled patterns
caption: Mac OS 9's desktop pictures finished at 4K (JPEG), AmigaOS 3.9's 30 backdrops and its 79 Workbench patterns as a collection each; a pattern is tiled at its own size, one texture pixel to a device pixel, at every scale (here Boing Chess at 1×). The HDR gain is a little more subtle (1.25 stops at most, from 2).

title: Performance: a kept core, realtime threads
caption: Preferences ▸ Performance ▸ Scheduler: "Keep a core for the window server" (on by default): app_server's loop and input thread have the fastest core to themselves and every other program runs on the others; Keep Them Off asks Olo Doctor to keep the system's services off it too. The kernel's own scheduler is the recommended one now: Olo's threads someone waits on are realtime under either.

title: Backgrounds: all of Mac OS 9's pictures and patterns
caption: Mac OS 9's CD extras as three collections (26 renders, 34 photographs, 21 Nostalgia pictures, 4K JPEGs finished with 4x-UltraSharp), its 111 desktop patterns and 20 Large Patterns as tiles (here Bossanova Bondi, tiled at its 256 points). Patterns made larger by the image model in a grid within its limits: strips get more tiles along their short side (3:1 at most), large tiles a smaller scale (its pixel budget).

title: Terminal follows a change of look at once
caption: Switching light/dark or the theme changed Terminal's window but not its screen, which kept the look before until something else drew it again: in dark mode its ground stayed white (left, before; right, after). The screens' view now follows the look itself.

title: Secondary text read easily; dark mode's check boxes outlined
caption: Each pair before (left) and after (right). Notes, file details and status lines were the disabled colour, about 3:1 against the panel; now at least 4.5:1 and still quieter than the text (Classic light and dark, Platinum dark). By night a check box's or radio button's well has a rim lighter than the panel, where its darker rim vanished (Classic, Platinum and BeOS dark; light mode as it was).

title: Backgrounds: Mac OS X 10.0–10.4's desktop pictures
caption: From the 10.0–10.4 install discs: each release's Aqua Blue and Graphite (here Tiger's), the Abstracts, Flows, Lines and Tiles, the Nature and Plants photographs, Tiger's Black & White, and the Ripples as tiles; 60 at 4K. Wide originals cropped and finished from their own pixels; 4:3 ones widened and their colours set back to the originals'; the Lines and Tiles never redrawn by the model.

title: Icons at 16 and 24 px drawn for their size
caption: Classic (top two rows) and Platinum (bottom two), before and after, magnified 4×: at 16 and 24 px every icon is sharpened a touch and gets a contour a pixel wide, as BeOS R5's mini icons had, so light things (pages, keyboards, the AirPods' case, the ruler) read on a light panel instead of fading into it.

title: Backgrounds: Windows 3.1, 95 and 98
caption: Windows 3.1's eleven tiles (here Argyle), Windows 95's Clouds and its thirteen tiles, and Windows 98's fifteen desktop pictures, their logos left out: 39 more in the pack, 445 in all. The pixel-art tiles made larger by nearest neighbour (one original pixel, exactly 2×2 device pixels at 2×); 95's photographic Forest and Sandstone by 4x-UltraSharp; 98's pictures widened to 4K and their colours set back to the originals'.

title: Backgrounds: CDE's backdrops, in CDE's own colours
caption: CDE's 24 backdrops (here KnitLight, workspace One's default) rendered as CDE drew them: the Default palette's colour sets, each colour's shadows by Motif's own arithmetic, workspace n's set {3, 5, 6, 7}, an XPM's symbolic colours from that set and a bitmap in its background on its bottom shadow (read from dtwm, dtsession and Motif's source). Tiles that aren't square now keep their shape (CDE's skies were one flat colour, Honey's hexagons squashed).

title: Backgrounds: Windows 2000's tiles
caption: Windows 2000's eleven tiles (here Gone Fishing): Blue Lace 16 and Zapotec made larger by nearest neighbour, the photographic nine (Coffee Bean, Feather Texture, Gone Fishing, Greenstone, Prairie Wind, Rhododendron, River Sumida, Santa Fe Stucco, Soap Bubbles) by 4x-UltraSharp's tile mosaic. 480 in the pack.

title: Backgrounds: OS/2 Warp 4's
caption: OS/2 Warp 4's backgrounds, from its CD's PACK2 bundles: its eight pictures (Garden, Garden 2, Ocean, Ocean 2 (here), Space, Space 2, Warp 03, Warp 04) redrawn at 4K, and its 35 textures (OS/2 Warp 4 Patterns: Big Blue, Burlap, Gold, Green Marble, Pool, Rice Mat, Wicker, Texture 1–12 …), their dither blurred away before 4x-UltraSharp. Its logos left out. 523 in the pack.

title: OS Updates: Fedora's packages, chosen and reviewed
caption: A new app, through DNF5's own daemon: every update with its check box (Choose: All · Security Updates · Bug Fixes · Enhancements · Other Updates · None, and Update 20), searched and filtered by kind, severity, repository and chosen, the most pressing first; the selected one's versions, sizes, advisories with their CVEs linked, and its changelog since what's installed. Each change is reviewed before it runs; Repositories, History with Undo and Upgrade Fedora beside it. (Against dnf-fake: made-up updates.)

title: Tracker: Compress and Extract
caption: Tracker compresses and extracts, natively (olo-archive, in Rust: zip with AES, tar with gzip, xz, zstd or bzip2, 7-Zip with AES; it reads RAR, ISO 9660 and cpio too): a selection's Compress ▸ makes an archive beside it, Compress As… names it, chooses its format and gives it a password; an archive's Extract Here and Extract To… take everything out (one thing as it is, several in a folder named for it), nothing written outside. Jobs with progress and Stop in Tracker Status, undone by Edit ▸ Undo; a password asked for when one is needed.

title: Tracker: an archive looked into as a folder
caption: Opening an archive in Tracker (zip, tar, 7-Zip, RAR, ISO, cpio) shows what's in it, a level at a time: folders open in the window (Enclosing Folder comes back out), a file opens with what opens its kind, taken out into Tracker's cache once; Extract Selected… takes what's selected out to a folder chosen, Extract All everything beside the archive. A password, when it has one, is asked for in the window.

title: Tracker: an archive's password, from Passwords
caption: An archive that wants a password offers Passwords: Use Saved Password reads the one kept for it (a Password item "Archive: NAME", asked only when pressed), Keep It in Passwords keeps the one typed once it has worked, and Compress As… keeps a new archive's password (on by default). The same in the archive's own window.

title: Tracker reads UDF disc images
caption: Windows' install images, DVDs and Blu-ray discs keep their files in a UDF tree; their ISO 9660 tree holds at most a note saying so. olo-archive reads UDF 1.02 to 2.60 now (its metadata partition, a write-once disc's virtual allocation table), so an image like this one, made by genisoimage, opens in Tracker with its long and Unicode names, and Extract takes them out.

title: Programs' Secrets asks with its words
caption: Olo's keyring prompter read every property of a gcr prompt as empty (each value is a variant in a variant), so olo-secrets' password prompts came up with no title or text. Now peeled: this one moves the keyring's key over from GNOME Keyring's file, read natively, once (light, 2x).

title: Programs' secrets locked: said, with Unlock
caption: Olo's keyring never stays locked in silence: when the login password isn't given (Not Now), or it can't be opened, a notification says so with Unlock…, which asks again (and it comes back while it stays locked). Programs asking for a secret bring the prompt too, but not again within two minutes of a Not Now; org.olo.Secrets1.Unlock asks over the bus (light, 2x).

title: Passwords: Approve Always, kept
caption: An app asking for an item by its reference (Weather's key) is asked about once: Approve Always (the default, Return) keeps it allowed across restarts and upgrades, in the vault, until taken back in File > Apps Allowed...; Approve Once is just this time; Deny (Escape). Before, an Allow lasted only until Passwords quit, so Weather asked again after every restart (light, 2x).

title: Passwords: Apps Allowed
caption: File > Apps Allowed... lists the apps allowed an item for good (Approve Always): the app, the item and since when, each with Take Back (the app is asked again the next time). Kept in the vault. Checked at 1x, 1.5x and 2x, light and dark; app_server no longer gives a returning dialog its app's group size (this one came back the main window's size, wider than the screen) (light, 2x).

title: Weather: the time axis stays at the top
caption: Weather's chart has its time axis over the panels now (the days, then the hours), and once the chart reaches the top of its scroll view the axis stays there as the panels scroll under it, so the hour of what's under the pointer is always in sight; in Next 7 Days it pins once the hourly chart comes up, never over the day rows. The kit's ScrollView::sticky and Timeline::axis do it for any app. Review clean at 1x, 1.5x, 2x; dark too (light, 2x).

title: Weather: ten questions to start with
caption: The assistant offers ten questions covering what people ask of a forecast most: rain (when it stops, while it rains), what to wear, how warm or cold, wind, storms, the weekend, the week, the sun, a time for a run, and Ben's own, "Will the clouds be high enough to skydive?". After five in the evening the day's become tomorrow's. A question wider than the column wraps (the kit's LinkButton::wrap_at), shown here at the window's least width (light, 2x).

title: Weather: a place's own name
caption: A kept place can have a name of its own (File > Rename Place..., or its right-click's Rename...): shown in the list, the title, Copy and what the assistant is told, with what it was found as beside it in the header; empty, it goes back to that name. Agents: rename:NAME, and place:NAME finds it by either name (light, 2x).

title: Weather: a place by its address
caption: Add Place finds street addresses as they're typed (Photon, OpenStreetMap's, made for search as you type), beside towns and airfields (Open-Meteo's): here a drop zone by its name, then by its address. A place found by its address is forecast for that point; its time zone and ground height are looked up once it's added, the dialog never waiting on it (light, 2x).

title: Terminal: a resume line with the options it was started with
caption: A program started with options (here a stand-in codex, --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox) prints how to resume without them; typing co suggests the resume with them carried over, learned from how the person runs their programs (which options take a value, which they always give it, whether they carry them), not a rule for any program. New commands are learned within a second (light, 2x).

title: Deskbar: Weather's widgets
caption: Weather gives Deskbar three widgets (Preferences > Deskbar, Add): Now (the sky and temperature, feels like and wind, what the next hour does), Next Hours (3, 6 or 12: six times across, each its sky and temperature, the chance of rain or the cloud as small columns) and Next Days (3, 5 or 7: each day's sky and its low to its high, cold to warm). Any app can give Deskbar widgets this way: it says what to show from each time on, and Olo draws it, so it goes on hour by hour with nothing running (light, 2x).

title: Deskbar: Weather's widgets, dark
caption: The same three widgets in the dark look: the day spans' colours run cold to warm in its own hues (dark, 2x).

title: Weather: places in your own order
caption: Places are dragged into the order you want (the kit's Sidebar::on_reorder: a line shows where the row will go among its section's rows), or moved with Move Up and Move Down on a place's menu; the place shown stays shown. Every place's sky and temperature now stay up to date by themselves, each fetched as its forecast gets old, without clicking it (light, 2x).

title: OS Updates: a package changing architecture no longer empties the update
caption: Updating everything chosen used to come to "Nothing to do" when one package's update moved between noarch and an architecture (python3-wcwidth): it was asked for by the new build's name and architecture, which dnf refuses, and one refused argument empties a whole transaction. Each update is now asked for as dnf names what's installed, and anything dnf still refuses is left out with a line saying so, so the rest goes ahead (here against the stand-in daemon, light, 2x).

title: Agent Screens: every screen's last use as it happens
caption: A screen's time in the sidebar moved on only when you clicked it: only the chosen screen's history was followed, the others' read only when screens came or went. Now every listed screen's history is followed (left: beta 20 min; middle: an agent acted on it, now, with no click), and every time said relative to now in Olo follows the clock by itself (right, a minute later: 2 min and 1 min). The kit's olo_kit::ago says it and the window draws again exactly when the words change, nothing in between (light, 2x).

title: Power: each SSD by its own name
caption: Power Modes named its NVMe row "SSD" ("SSD 1", "SSD 2" with more), which said nothing of which drive is which. Each is named by its model now (here SKHynix HFS002TFM9X179N, cut with its whole name in the tip), with its size, then its device, added only where two would read alike; the summary line says it too. Each was already set on its own, by its serial (light, 2x).

title: Kache: the build cache's status
caption: A new app for kache (our fork): the service and its buttons (Clean Up Now, Restart, Stop), the store against its limit, the last 24 hours' hit rate and time saved, the pool's slots now, and builds by the hour. The demo (OLO_KACHE_DEMO), light, 2×.

title: Kache in dark at 1.5×
caption: Status in dark mode at 1.5×: the same cards, the chart's hues from the palette.

title: Kache: builds
caption: The projects built most and the slowest compiles over the day, then each build: when, crate, project, result, how long, how big.

title: Kache: kache's settings
caption: The [cache] keys worth tuning, each field showing what kache does when it's left empty and what it is beside it; saved into config.toml keeping its comments. Dark, 1×.

title: Kache's Deskbar widget
caption: Build Cache: the day's hit rate, the pool's slots in use, and the last 6 hours (builds, and a bar of the share that were hits). Slots without icons now drop the kit's icon row. 1× (doubled), 1.5×, 2×.

title: Power: SATA SSDs, each by its name
caption: Preferences ▸ Power ▸ Power Modes with a SATA SSD beside the NVMe drive (its link's power: Cooler naps, Coolest sleeps), the names' column as wide as the longest name, and the three modes side by side so the tab fits 1280 × 800. The made-up machine (OLO_POWER_DEMO), light, 2×.

title: Kache: settings as sliders
caption: Every setting a slider over its valid steps alone, its value said with its unit, kache's own first; the store's on the left, the pool's on the right, in rows that start level. Dark, 2×.

title: Kache: why misses missed
caption: Builds: each miss with its cause (from kache's key fields: the first part that changed against the same crate's last build with the same flags), and the day's causes counted.

title: Kache: tests holding slots
caption: Status: the tests holding the pool's slots (read from the kernel's list of locks), each with End.

title: Auto-tiling: Columns, Rows, Grid and Spiral
caption: Four more auto-tiling layouts, as the best-known tiling window managers have them (Amethyst's Column and Row, xmonad's Grid, awesome's and bspwm's Spiral): Doctor, Logs, Disk Usage and Styled Edit on a 2560 × 1600 display, in Columns, Rows (Disk Usage keeps its least height), Grid and Spiral. Chosen per workspace from Deskbar's tray, or round them all with Ctrl+Alt+Cmd+Space; the windows keep their order from one layout to the next.

title: Deskbar: the layouts, grouped
caption: Deskbar's Auto-Tiling Layout menu with the new layouts: Main and Stack's three first, then Halves, Columns, Rows, Grid and Spiral (1.5×).

title: Deskbar: Number of Main Windows
caption: Main and Stack can have several main windows sharing the main place (dwm's and xmonad's nmaster), chosen for each display's workspace from Deskbar's tray, or one more and one fewer with Ctrl+Alt+Cmd+I and D (1.5×).

title: Preferences: the number of main windows
caption: Preferences ▸ Windows sets how many main windows a workspace starts with; the miniature shows two sharing the left two thirds (1.5×).

title: Preferences: no space around a window alone
caption: Smart gaps, as i3 and sway have them: with the box checked, an auto-tiled window alone on its display fills it, no margin or gap; they come back with a second tile (1×).

title: Preferences: where new windows go
caption: New windows go first (as the main window), after the active window, or last, in Main and Stack and the layouts built in order; Halves always halves the active tile (1×).

title: Window menu: All Workspaces and the scratchpad
caption: A window can be shown on every workspace of its display (BeOS's All Workspaces, i3's sticky windows: it floats) or put in the scratchpad (i3's and sway's: hidden, floating, brought over the active workspace by Ctrl+Alt+Cmd+Minus and hidden again), from its window menu or by keys (1.5×).

title: Window menu: an app's own workspace
caption: Always Open StyledEdit on Workspace 1: an app's new windows open on a workspace of their own (i3's assign, Hyprland's workspace rules), on the display they open on, without it going there; chosen again, as any app's (1.5×).

title: Preferences: apps with their own workspace
caption: Preferences ▸ Windows lists the apps whose new windows open on a workspace of their own; unchecking one opens its windows where you are again (1.5×).

title: Auto-tiling: preselecting where the next window goes
caption: Ctrl+Shift+Cmd+J on a tile: the next window opens below it, the half it will take tinted in the keyboard-navigation colour till then (bspwm's preselection, i3's split before a window opens); the same keys again take it back (1.5×).

title: Auto-tiling: Scrolling, niri's columns
caption: Scrolling lays windows out as columns of their own widths in a strip, scrolled to the active one (niri's, PaperWM's). Here Logs and Doctor at two thirds: Doctor's column goes past the first display's edge, cut there; the second display (right) shows its own desktop, not the column (2560 × 1440 and 1920 × 1200, 1×, half size).

title: Preferences: the Scrolling layout
caption: Preferences ▸ Windows with Scrolling chosen: the miniature shows columns half the display wide, scrolled to the middle one, cut at the room beside Deskbar (1×).

title: Olo Doctor suggests removing the build kept from before the kits
caption: A build kept to fall back to (tools/keep-build.sh) from before Olo's own kits runs GPUI, which is gone for good: Doctor suggests removing it and its login screen entry, with its size, never the session running. Here with a stand-in kept build; the number and its unit stay on one line now that the kit's wrapping keeps a no-break space whole.

title: A button showing the long job it started
caption: Button::working: a button that started a job of five seconds or more shows its progress on itself while it can't be pressed again: the status bar's sunken well filled as far as it's got, the label over it readable on both parts, or a band sweeping across when how far isn't known. Here at rest, at 0, 42%, 100%, unknown and on a default button (the kit's working example). Agent Screens' Export Video… and Kache's Clean Up Now use it.

title: Olo Doctor keeps the desktop's memory in memory
caption: Three findings beside the one for windows' graphics memory (Ben, 2026-11-16, after a stall while typing): Keep the Core in Memory (app_server, Deskbar and the session lock their own memory; the sound server is never swapped), Keep Programs in Memory (swappiness 1) and, as a suggestion, swap as large as memory. Each sets itself up from its button.

title: Sound: a quiet microphone's boost, suggested from how loud the voice comes in
caption: Preferences ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Processing has a boost for each microphone, in 3 dB steps. The voice service measures the voice's level as something records (its active speech level), the panel says it and what would bring it to the -26 dB aimed for, and Use Suggested sets that; Try It tries the suggested boost beside the other settings (Ben, 2026-11-16: some inputs like AirPods are not loud enough).

title: Olo Doctor offers BBRv3 for TCP
caption: A new suggestion, "TCP could send with BBRv3": Use BBRv3 puts in Olo's module (Google's BBRv3 made for the kernel as it comes) and the service that builds and loads it at every start. Its text says what the congestion control in use does and what was measured (45.8 Mbit/s to CUBIC's 47.1 on a 50 Mbit/s link, with the round trip at 43 ms where CUBIC's was 69).

title: Network Speed Test
caption: A new app: what the connection carries each way, and everything that can be measured or read of it. Four cards (Download, Upload, Latency, Connection), each a figure, a graph and its facts, live as the test runs: the round trip idle and while the line is busy and what the busy line adds, what TCP sent again (this computer's kernel's count going up, the server's coming down), the congestion control and BBR's model of the path, what arrived out of order, how long the name, TCP and TLS took, the link. (Made-up results here.)

title: Preferences ▸ Performance ▸ Kernel
caption: A new tab for the kernel's settings Olo suggests and Olo's own pieces in the kernel, each with its switch, what it does and its figures as they are: full preemption and a limit on what waits in memory for a removable disk (the two settings that measured as a gain with nothing given up: kernel/TUNING.md), BBRv3 with the connections on it now, and the graphics-memory live patch. A switch has Olo Doctor set it, as root; the figures are read while the tab is shown. (A made-up computer.)

title: Olo Doctor suggests two kernel settings
caption: Full preemption ("Preempt at Once") and a limit on what waits in memory for a removable disk ("Limit Removable Disks"), each with what was measured for it on this kernel in a KVM guest. They are the two of everything the desktop kernels are known for that gained something here with nothing given up; the rest is in Fedora's kernel already, can't be had without replacing it, or was measured and left alone (kernel/TUNING.md).

title: Viewer: a PDF's pictures at full quality
caption: A PDF page that is one large picture (slides exported at 3840 × 2160) was shown soft and with breaks: the renderer dropped a column and a row of a picture drawn smaller and filtered it softly; Viewer left a page stretched when its zoom moved by a fraction of a percent; the kit drew a tile a pixel wider than it is at 1.5×; and a page past the size cap was drawn over part of its place. Now what the window shows is the renderer's output pixel for pixel at every scale, and that is an exact Lanczos resampling of the picture. (A made-up slide, three times enlarged.)

title: Viewer: Presentation, Full Screen and keys for a PDF's pages
caption: Presentation (View ▸ Presentation, ⇧⌘P or P) leaves the window with nothing in it but the page: no menu bar, no tool bar, no scroll bars, and the window takes the page's own shape, so it can be shared as it is in a call or over AirPlay. Full Screen (F) is the same on the whole screen. In both a PDF is a page at a time: the arrows, Space, Return, Page Up and Down, Home and End, a wheel's notch or a click turn the pages, Escape leaves. Next, Previous, First and Last Page, Fit Width and Fit Page have keys in the menus. (A made-up deck.)

title: The new brand: the mark, and the wordmark set in Sora
caption: Olo's brand sheet followed (docs/BRAND.md): the mark drawn again by the icon model against the sheet's, and the wordmark set from Sora by tools/mkbrand.py (Olo in ExtraBold with its l a plain bar, DESKTOP in SemiBold tracked 320), never drawn. The horizontal and stacked logos, the wordmark and Olo alone, for light and for dark.

title: The brand in Olo: About, Deskbar's tile and Themes
caption: About shows the mark and Olo in Sora; Deskbar's tile is the mark alone (beside the wordmark it read as O Olo); Preferences ▸ Themes shows each theme's own mark beside its name (Platinum's drawn again too), the wordmark being the same in every theme now.

title: Deskbar's tile at 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 and 2×, light and dark
caption: The Olo mark alone, 24 points, centred on whole pixels at every scale (magnified).

title: The upgrade's veil and the start-up screen with the logo
caption: The horizontal logo on dark (the mark, a rule, Olo DESKTOP) where the old wordmark was, pre-scaled for each scale and drawn pixel for pixel; the boot splash is the same picture (Olo Doctor offers to draw an installed one again).

title: Olo's own wallpapers: Orbit, Halo, Ribbons, Shapes, Glass, Dunes
caption: Six abstract 4K pictures in Olo blue and Olo yellow, drawn by the image model from words alone; under them the dark versions of Orbit, Shapes, Glass and Dunes.

title: Every wallpaper restored: bands, blotches and JPEG's blocks gone
caption: Contrast stretched to show it: the image model's 8-bit bands and mottling in Halo's dark sky, and JPEG's blocks in a gradient of AmigaOS's Simplify, before and after tools/restorewallpaper.py. All 559 pictures and tiles of the pack, restored only where they are smooth, and kept as lossless WebP.

title: Speed Test floats at its own size, and is called Speed Test
caption: Network Speed Test is now Speed Test, and its window is the size of what it shows and no other: it floats over tiled windows and is never a tile or a tab. Tiled, it was stretched to a window its four cards filled a corner of, its menu bar stopping where they did. (Here with auto-tiling on: StyledEdit's window has the tile, Speed Test floats over it.)

title: A code texted to the phone, offered in the tab waiting for it
caption: With BlueFerry's backend installed (Olo Doctor offers it) and an iPhone paired, a one-time code that arrives by text message is found as it comes and offered under the field of the browser tab that is waiting for it: Fill code, who it is from. A click takes it, or Down then Return. Olo's phone service asks every browser which tabs are waiting and chooses among them; a tab on an Agent Screen gets it put in at once when it surely is that tab's, and the person is told. (A made-up bank and code, a stand-in phone.)

title: Preferences ▸ Phone
caption: The new Phone panel: how the iPhone stands (its battery, which of its services are up, how many conversations and unread), what is told of (each message in a notification of Olo's own that can be answered in place, everything the phone notifies of, or nothing), and where one-time codes go: offered in the browser tab waiting for one, and in an agent's tab put in at once, asked about first, or never. Without the backend it leads to Olo Doctor, which installs BlueFerry; without a phone, to pairing. (A stand-in phone.)

title: The phone in Deskbar's tray
caption: While an iPhone is connected (or has messages unread, or a one-time code has just come) it is in Deskbar's tray: a phone, dim when it is out of reach, amber and red as its battery runs down, with a dot while messages are unread. Its menu says how it stands, copies the code that just came, and opens Preferences ▸ Phone. (A stand-in phone.)

title: Quick Look copies, selects all and finds
caption: Tracker's Quick Look had no keys of its own beyond Space and the arrows: Copy did nothing. It now has Copy (what is selected of a text, else the file itself), Select All and Find, by key, in the command palette and for agents; and typing in its find field no longer loses the letters and the space the window takes for itself. (Here, a text with all of it selected.)

title: Setting up an iPhone, a step at a time
caption: How do I set up my iPhone? Preferences ▸ Phone now says, and does each step from where it is: Install BlueFerry (the button has Olo Doctor install it; no trip to Doctor), Pair the iPhone (the pairing opens), and what to turn on on the phone; each step ticked as it is done, the one to do next in bold with its button. A phone in Bluetooth's list has Messages and Codes…, which opens the same panel. (A stand-in backend, no phone paired.)

title: Connecting a phone, natively: find it
caption: Olo now speaks to an iPhone or an Android phone itself, in Rust (OBEX, the Message Access and Phone Book Access profiles over channels BlueZ opens); BlueFerry is gone. Preferences ▸ Phone connects one in three steps, each seen to happen: here the first, the phones nearby with Pair. (A stand-in phone and a stand-in BlueZ.)

title: Connecting a phone: the code, large
caption: The second step: the same six digits on the computer and on the phone, shown large in two groups, with It Matches (Return) and It's Different. (Building it found that Olo's pairing agent hung on every question a device asked: fixed.)

title: Connecting a phone: its own switches
caption: The third step: the phone's own switches for this computer, drawn as the phone shows them (an iPhone's Show Notifications and Sync Contacts; an Android's Text messages and Contacts). Each turns green as the phone turns it on; the page follows by itself.

title: Bluetooth: room for a phone's buttons
caption: A phone chosen in Preferences ▸ Bluetooth has four buttons, and the last was cut off (Ben's screenshot); the panel is wider, its columns too, and the layout lint now sees it with a phone chosen, so it can't happen again. The phone's button is now "Phone Settings…".

title: Phone, the app
caption: The phone's conversations in a window, as Telegram's: who, their latest words and how many unread down the left; the conversation as balloons (ours in a tint of the keyboard's blue, runs joined, a heading for each day), and the field to write in. It asks the phone service for everything and holds nothing itself. (Made-up people: the demo.)

title: Phone: a one-time code, in the dark look
caption: A message with a one-time code has Copy under it. Dark, as every Olo app.

title: Phone: the contacts
caption: The phone's contacts, with a search over them; one number is written to at a click, several show the contact's card. A number typed in the search can be written to with no contact.

title: Viewer: a long video's times have their room
caption: A video over an hour has longer times (2:22:06 of 2:45:18, here at 2×), and the bar started under the time played. The bar now sits between the two times, each given the room of its widest.

title: Deskbar: the phone's tray glyph, the size of the others
caption: The phone in Deskbar's tray was taller than its cell and off to the right; it's 8 by 14 points in the middle of it now, level with its neighbours. A dot while messages are unread.

title: Olo Doctor: everything it does can be undone
caption: What Doctor fixed is listed under Fixed with when, what undoing does, and Undo: the file as it was, the service as it stood, the packages it added removed. What can't be put back (an update) is said. (Made-up entries, in a test.)

title: The start-up sound: a quarter of full volume, silent when muted
caption: Olo's start-up sound plays at a quarter of the output's full volume whatever your volume is, and not at all while the sound is muted, as a session starts and as the computer does. Preferences ▸ Sound says so under it; Play goes by it too.

title: Phone: what the phone is playing, with Play, Next and Previous
caption: Phone shows what the phone is playing under the list, with Previous, Pause or Play and Next; Deskbar's phone menu has them too, and olo-phone --music. The phone stays the player: Olo is its remote control. (Sample data.)

title: Phone: an iPhone's other notifications, with their actions
caption: An iPhone's notifications show on the computer: every app's, calls among them, with Answer and Decline or Clear, which act on the phone; one dealt with on the phone goes here too. (A stand-in phone, in a test.)

title: Phone: a call answered on the computer
caption: Answer on a ringing call's notification takes the call on the computer: Olo connects the phone hands-free for that call, answers it, shows it with Hang Up, and lets the phone go after. Phone's contacts have Call. (A stand-in phone, in a test.)

title: Classic's wallpaper is the Dunes
caption: A new install, and the Classic theme when chosen, start with Olo's own Dunes, by day and by night. (It was Mac OS 9's Blueberry Oxygen, still in the pack.)

title: Preferences ▸ Terminal: Choose… for the worktrees' folder
caption: The folder New Worktree… makes worktrees in can be chosen in a folder panel, with Choose… beside the field.

title: Focus: no zoom box on a window's tab
caption: In Focus every window is zoomed already, so its tab has no zoom box: the tab is narrower and the title has its room. (Above: Standard; below: Focus.)

title: A paired phone's own picture: twenty phones, in both icon themes
caption: The ten commonest iPhones and the ten commonest Android phones, each from behind (its colour, its cameras), in Classic and Platinum. The paired phone shows as the nearest to what it says it is, in Preferences ▸ Phone, Deskbar's phone menu and Phone.

title: Viewer and Quick Look: the text in a picture, selected and copied
caption: A picture's text is read where it's shown: drag over it to select, ⌘C copies it, ⌘A selects it all. (Above: a word dragged over; below: Select All.)

title: Tiling: the main window can be pinned
caption: Pin as Main (⌃⌥⇧⌘M, a window's menu, Deskbar) keeps a tile the main one of Main and Stack: windows that open take the stack's places. Making another main by hand lets it go.

title: Tracker: a picture's icon is the picture
caption: In the icon view (and on the desktop) pictures show as themselves and a video as a frame of it, made as they scroll into view and kept in the desktop's thumbnail cache. (Left 1×, right 2×.)

title: Website: Terminal and coding agents
caption: Five new rows in the website's Agents part (tab titles and groups, Keep It Going, Auto Approve, worktrees, Preferences), each with a picture from tools/dev/readme-shots terminal-agents. Also fixed on the way: --help opens no window, a hover-opened submenu keeps the keyboard, open menus are in olo-screen's tree, a window comes back to its own place.

title: Smart tiling with a model, removed
caption: Smart Tile is gone: its program, shortcut, Deskbar item and its box in Preferences ▸ AI (the panel now: Models, Ask, Weather; Emoji, Agent Screens, Claude Code).

title: File panels: Go to File or Folder
caption: Every Open, Save and folder panel opens Tracker's Go to File or Folder by its keys (⇧⌘G), or by a / or ~ typed in the list. Left: a path typed with Tab completing; right: the panel there, the file selected.

title: A window tab's menu: Hide ▸ and Close ▸
caption: A tab of a window group has Hide ▸ (Hide, Hide Others, Hide All) and Close ▸ (Close, Close Others, Close All), acting on the group's windows.

title: Passwords: a page's one-time code QR
caption: A page setting up two-step sign-in shows a QR code; Passwords' Chrome extension notices it, Passwords reads it and asks whether to add it to the site's login (here: replace the one it has).

title: Viewer and Quick Look: a PowerPoint's slides, drawn
caption: A presentation showed as a list of Slide 1 to Slide 4 headings. Now each slide is drawn as it looks (its shapes, text, pictures, tables, its master's and theme's), natively, one under another, for the pixels it covers. (A deck made for the tests.)

title: Themes: Catppuccin and the ten most installed editor colour schemes
caption: Preferences ▸ Themes ▸ Colors has thirteen schemes from elsewhere beside the theme's own and BeOS's, each light and dark and tuned for Olo; Terminal follows the one chosen, or keeps its own. Here Tokyo Night, at night.

title: A window tab's menu: Pin, an app's windows always in one place
caption: Pin has Always Main and Always [the part the window is in now], here Always Top Right Quarter for Tracker in a grid of four tiles. The pin is the app's: its window goes there on whichever display and workspace it opens, and stays in the nearest tile as others come and go.

title: Passwords in Chrome: an authenticator's code, offered under the field
caption: A field waiting for a one-time code, on a site whose login in Passwords has one, is offered the code as a texted one is; taken, the code good at that moment goes in. (A page and a login made for the test.)

title: Deskbar: a blue dot for notifications, a red one for what's unread in the app
caption: No number beside the blue dot any more; left of it, a red dot while the app says something is unread or waiting in it (here Terminal has both, StyledEdit a notification, the Viewer something unread), at 1×, 1.5× and 2×. Their colours are the look's own.

title: Every icon a drawing
caption: Classic's 181 icons are hand-written SVG drawings now, rendered for the exact pixels they're shown at (here 1.5×): one projection, one outline, the same forms throughout. They replace pictures shrunk from 256 pixels.

title: Platinum's icons: the same drawings, its colours
caption: A theme without a drawing of its own shows the classic one in its colours (Platinum: black ink, lilac greys, a lilac-blue folder, periwinkle blues), so an icon has the same angle, size and detail in every theme.

title: The start-up veil's icons are drawn for their size
caption: The veil and the boot splash show Olo's drawings, rendered for the slot's own pixels at 1×, 1.5× and 2× (they were the nearest pre-scaled picture no bigger than the slot).

title: Deskbar's Inbox widget: notifications and what waits in apps, as cards
caption: A stack of cards to work through, newest on top: its app, a red dot (its app is waiting for you) or a blue one (news), the title and text, and Previous, Next, Snooze and Dismiss. Slack counts three and one of them has its notification in the stack: that card is red too, and this one says the two more.

title: Terminal's welcome: the ring, this computer, a haiku
caption: Olo Doctor suggests it. A new shell opens with Olo's ring drawn in the terminal's cells from its own drawing, what the computer is and how it's doing (memory, disk and battery as bars), the terminal's colours, and one of twenty-four haiku.

title: Themes: one list, a preview with the theme's own icons, Customize…
caption: Classic, Platinum, BeOS and every scheme are themes in one list (26), each with its colours, its icon set and its wallpaper. The preview shows the theme's window, its icons and its wallpaper; Customize… changes any colour, the icon set and the wallpaper.

title: AmigaOS: a theme after Workbench 3, its icons in sixteen pens
caption: Workbench's grey, black, white and blue, flat and square; the same drawings as every set, each face flat and in one of a Workbench screen's sixteen pens, outlined in black.

title: Aqua: a theme after Mac OS X's first Aqua, its icons shinier and bluer
caption: Bright white panels, gel blue and deep gloss; the same drawings with rounder, shinier faces, Aqua's blues, and soft deep-blue outlines in place of black.

title: Flat: an icon set of its own drawings, seen straight on
caption: 176 drawings, each thing front-facing in plain flat faces, no outlines or shadows, made from shared forms (tools/dev/flaticons). Chosen for any theme in Preferences ▸ Themes ▸ Customize… ▸ Icons; here on Classic.

title: Other people's marks, drawn for every icon set
caption: Chrome, Slack, Telegram and GitHub drawn again: the mark itself, on a badge or tile that leans half as much as the set's other standing things (left: the old ones and the new among Terminal, Tracker, Phone and Passwords at Deskbar's sizes). Each icon set has its own: classic, Platinum, BeOS, AmigaOS, Aqua and, straight on, Flat. Slack's tile no longer loses its mark at 40 pixels (a 2× screen): a size between two steps shows the drawing's small stand-in.

title: Deskbar: dividers among the widgets
caption: A new kind of widget that shows nothing of the computer: room, a line or a heading, to set groups of widgets apart. Here a heading with an etched line, a thin line, a dotted one edge to edge, a short row of dots, a heading in a hue with a thick line, and room alone. Preferences ▸ Deskbar ▸ Add ▸ Divider.

title: The bell's count in a colour of your own
caption: Preferences ▸ Notifications ▸ Deskbar ▸ The bell's count in: the look's own red, or any of the look's hues (here blue, yellow, green, purple, grey and orange, in a light and a dark look). The number is white, or near black where white would be lost.

title: Notifications: an archive
caption: What leaves the list (faded away, dismissed, cleared, forgotten) now goes to an archive, kept for 30 days. The link at the status bar's right, Archived (2), shows it, and Notifications (5) there goes back; so does View ▸ Archived. Rows there open what they were about or are deleted; Empty Archive and Undo.

title: The supervisor says when the laptop's controller floods the system
caption: When the embedded controller reports the same power event over and over (as a ThinkPad P1's did for two hours), the supervisor now notices within seconds and says so in a notification that stays, and Olo Doctor has the whole account as a Critical finding. Shown here with a made-up storm.

title: Deskbar folds away to the right
caption: A small button at Deskbar's top right (two chevrons) folds it away: only that button stays, at the screen's corner, and zoomed and tiled windows take the room; a click on it brings Deskbar back and the windows make way. Above, Deskbar with a zoomed Tracker beside it; below, folded.

title: Calendar: every calendar in one, by day, week, month and as an agenda
caption: A new app, olo-calendar, on the engine made this week (iCalendar, repeating events, CalDAV for Google's and Fastmail's accounts). The small month and the calendars at the left, each in one of the look's own colours; Day, Week, Month and Agenda; the present a line across today. It shows and doesn't change anything yet: the editor is next. Seen here with its demo calendars.

title: A window's tab at each display's own size, part way between two
caption: Dragged from a display to one of another scale, a window's tab showed at the first display's size on the second (twice as big from 2× to 1×). app_server kept one look of the tab and showed it whatever it was drawn for; now it keeps a look a scale. Here a window held across a 1.5× screen and a 2× one, each side enlarged to the same size: the tab runs straight across the seam.

title: Calendar: events made, changed and deleted
caption: The event's window (here in the dark): title, where, calendar, all day or from when to when as you'd write it (Nov 20, fri, 2:30pm), how it repeats, a reminder, notes. Changing one of a repeating event asks: only this one, or every one of them. Written to the calendar's server first, and never over a change made somewhere else.

title: Preferences ▸ Integrations ▸ Calendars: accounts for Calendar
caption: Add an Account… ▸ Google…, Fastmail… or Another CalDAV Server…. Google's is a sign-in in the browser with your own client (the one DiskBackup's Drive set-up made is found by itself; here none is, so its ID and secret are asked for); Fastmail's an app password. What's typed is tried first, then kept in the login keyring; Calendar shows the account's calendars the moment it's added.

title: Calendar's icon
caption: A block calendar standing: a red binding over a leaf of days, one of them today. Drawn for each size (at 16 pixels, four days; at 32, six; the whole month from 48), in the set's projection and light; below it in Platinum's, BeOS's, AmigaOS's and Aqua's colours, and the Flat set's own drawing, straight on.

title: Calendar's reminders
caption: An event's reminders show at their time, from a service the session keeps (no window needed): the title, its calendar, how far off it is and when, where. Show opens Calendar on the day with the event selected. One missed while the computer slept still shows while its event isn't over.

title: A mailed sign-in link, offered
caption: Some services mail a button, not a code (Claude's "Your secure link to Claude is here"). The Olo extension now offers it under the field of the page that's waiting, as it offers a code: who it's from, that it came by mail, and where it goes. Taking it takes the tab there.

title: The extension's list: choose, then Fill or Open Passwords
caption: The toolbar button's list of this page's logins now has a selection (a click, the arrows): Fill fills it (Return, or a double click), and Open Passwords shows that login in Passwords. A field's menu has Passwords ▸ Check for Codes, and a code or sign-in link that came by mail says which account it came to.

title: Deskbar: other displays, collapsed
caption: An option in Preferences ▸ Deskbar (off unless turned on): each other display is one row in a display's Deskbar, with how many applications it has and an arrow. Down shows its workspaces and applications; up puts them away. Left and middle: Display 1 opened, light and dark; right: Display 0 collapsed, on the other display's Deskbar.

title: Calendar: an event dragged to another time
caption: Among the week's or the day's hours an event is pressed and dragged: it goes by quarter hours to the day under the pointer, drawn there with the times it would have while where it was goes faint (left). Let go, it's there (right). A repeating one asks whether only that one moves.

title: Calendar: Undo and Redo
caption: Every change in Calendar can be taken back and made again: Edit ▸ Undo and Redo, named for the step. Above: Dentist deleted, the deletion undone, redone, then (undone again) dragged to Thursday, and the move undone. Deleting an event no longer asks first.

title: Calendar: Find
caption: Calendar has a search field (⌘F). What's typed is looked for, as it's typed, in every calendar shown from a year back to two years on: titles, places and notes. What's found is listed by day, starting at today; the arrows step through it, Return (or two clicks) goes to the event in the view, Escape ends the search.

title: Calendar: an event's end is dragged
caption: An event's bottom edge can be dragged to change when it ends: the pointer turns to an up-and-down arrow over the edge, the end follows it by quarter hours with the times shown, and letting go saves it (Undo takes it back).

title: Calendar: events are dragged among the days
caption: In the month, and in the week's all-day strip, an event is dragged to other days: it keeps its time and its length, where it was stays faint, and where it would go is drawn across its days (here the Conference dragged across a week's end, and Release 2.4 from Thursday to Monday). A moved event stays selected.

title: Calendar: invitations
caption: An invitation shows what you answered: not answered is pale with a line round it (Interview), declined is struck through (Budget call), accepted looks like any event. Edit ▸ Reply answers the one selected (Yes, Maybe, No), and so does Going in its window, which lists the guests with each one's answer. Also: the SSD rows' "As It Is" in Preferences ▸ Power is now called Auto.

title: Calendar in Deskbar: Next Event and The Day Ahead
caption: Calendar gives Deskbar two widgets (Preferences ▸ Deskbar): what's next, with what comes after it, and the day ahead as a list in each calendar's colour. A click opens Calendar on the event. Their headline is ordinary-sized words, not the big figure Weather uses. Also: several files chosen in the file picker are handed to the program in name order.

title: Calendar's events in the command palette
caption: Type two letters or more in the palette and the events with those words in their title, place or notes are among the results, each at its next occurrence (or its last, if it's over), with when, where and which calendar. Return opens Calendar on it.

title: Calendar: an assistant
caption: View ▸ Show Assistant: ask about your calendars and it answers from the events of the ones you show, with links that go to the events it means. Asked to add or plan something, it drafts the event and a click opens it for you to look over and save: it never adds anything itself. Its model is in Preferences ▸ AI ▸ Calendar.

title: Notifications, made plain (first step)
caption: Unread is blue everywhere: the dot beside an app, on a card, in the list, and now the bell's count too. Nothing unread goes away by itself any more: only what you've read is tidied away, an hour after you read it. × clears, wherever it is (a banner's too). Archived is now Cleared, and each row there says why it left: cleared by you, tidied away, withdrawn by its app, replaced, or made room.

title: Notifications, made plain (second step): red is what waits in an app
caption: What an app says is waiting in it (Slack's 3 unread) is no longer an item among the notifications. It has a red dot beside the app in Deskbar, a row under Waiting in apps at the top of the Notifications window (a click goes to the app), and a red card in the Inbox with Later in place of ×. Notifications are always blue; the bell counts only them. Deskbar remembers apps' counts across an upgrade.

title: Notifications, made plain (third step): urgent is not an error
caption: An urgent notification (a call) stays on screen and comes through Do Not Disturb, without the stop sign: that is only for what says it failed (Backup failed, right). And a notification from the app you are already in is read as it arrives, with no banner over what you're looking at. Urgent and sticky banners come back after an upgrade.

title: Notifications, made plain (last step)
caption: When more banners arrive than fit, a line under them says how many are waiting, and a click on it opens the list. Also: a notification an app replaces after closing it no longer shows twice, and Olo's own apps have their icons on notifications sent by name.

title: Fans: a row of each power mode
caption: Preferences ▸ Power ▸ Power Modes has a Fans row: Auto (the computer's own), Cool, Cooler or Coolest for each mode, and on battery. Switching power modes switches the fans' profile. What was called Cool is Cooler now (the same curve), so what you had chosen is unchanged; the Fans box has left Battery & Idle.

title: The clock's menu: what the day holds
caption: A click on Deskbar's date and time opens a menu: the day in full, what's still to come today and tomorrow in Calendar (each in its calendar's colour; choose one to open Calendar on it), Open Calendar, and Date & Time Settings…, which is what the click did before.

title: Calendar: invite people to an event
caption: An event of your own has an Invite field: type your guests' addresses with commas between and Save. Your calendar's server sends the invitations, and the window lists each guest with what they've answered. Take an address out to uninvite.

title: One Google integration, and a grid of what each account is for
caption: Preferences ▸ Integrations ▸ Google: each Google account connected through an app of its own, “Olo (its address)”, which an agent makes for you in Google Cloud (Add a Google Account…). Tick Mail, Calendar and DiskBackup for each. DiskBackup's older app can be brought in as it is (Bring It Into Olo…), so its backups stay where they are.

title: DiskBackup says when it's paused, and its backups stay listed
caption: DiskBackup's window says Paused (or Waiting for power, or for the network) with when the last backup was, and Resume takes Back Up Now's place. A paused DiskBackup still lists its backups and can restore from them: pausing only stops it backing up and sending.

title: Language & Region in Preferences
caption: Preferences ▸ Language & Region chooses the language Olo's words are in, each language by its own name, and says how much of Olo is in it so far. Olo's windows change at once; other programs take it as they next start. The translations are coming, German first.

title: Integrations: a tab for each provider, Fastmail's like Google's
caption: Preferences ▸ Integrations has a tab for each of Google, Fastmail, CalDAV, GitHub and Telegram. Fastmail's lists its accounts as Google's does, each ticked for Mail and Calendar, with one app password each; the Fastmail accounts Mail and Calendar kept before move there by themselves after the upgrade.

title: Calendar: a preview pane
caption: One click on an event shows it in the bottom third of the main column: its title after its calendar's colour, Edit… at the right, its facts (when on the person's clock and on its own, where as a link, calendar, repeats, reminder, answer, guests) in a box beside its notes. View ▸ Show Preview.

title: Deskbar: other workspaces start collapsed
caption: With Preferences ▸ Deskbar ▸ "Other workspaces’ applications start collapsed", every Deskbar keeps open the workspace each display shows; each other one is its heading, how many applications it has and an arrow that shows them. Two displays' Deskbars.

title: DiskBackup: only when connected to Ethernet
caption: Schedule ▸ When to Back Up gains "Only when connected to Ethernet" under the battery's. Ticked, nothing is backed up without a wired connection; the window says "Waiting for Ethernet", and a backup under way when the cable comes out goes on once it's back.

title: Olo in French
caption: Preferences ▸ Keyboard ▸ Shortcuts with Olo's language set to French: every one of Olo's words has a French translation, set as French sets it (a narrow space before a colon). The profile row's menu now takes only the room its buttons leave, so a longer Delete never runs out of the box.

title: Disk Usage at its least size
caption: Before (left) and after: at its least window size, the list now has room for all its columns (Files was cut, with a scroll bar under it), and the chart's middle keeps room for its words (a small chart's rings narrower for it).

title: Olo's words, whole
caption: DiskBackup's first window in English and French. Olo's word list now has every app's words (its menus and windows, 2,259 of them; the first list had only Preferences' and DiskBackup's settings), German, Spanish and French each every one. Where the longer words ran out of room the layouts now follow them: these two boxes as tall as the taller, their buttons level.

title: DiskBackup's header: the paragraphs under the title take the whole width
caption: The title now shares a row with Restore and Back Up Now (centred on its line), and what's said under it (where it backs up to, the last backup, an unfinished one) runs the window's width beneath both. It used to wrap beside the buttons, which in German and French ran a line or two longer and past the window's foot. The schedule's choices are whole phrases after 'Automatically,' ('every hour'), so each language says them its own way, and each column of kept-backup menus lines up after its longer label. Its words, and the service's own (why it isn't backing up, an error), are now in German, Spanish and French.

title: Weather in German: the forecast, its cards and charts in the person's language
caption: Weather's precipitation and sky (tomorrow.io's 94 codes, each built in each language), its cards' titles and captions, its charts' legends and the next-hour line now follow Olo's language, and so do its assistant's suggested questions. The kit's dashboard cards, facts and chart legends look their words up as they're made. Captions were measured against their card and reworded where German ran past. Weekday names wait for Olo's formats.

title: Three laptop power modes
caption: Battery Saver stretches the remaining charge. Adaptive Performance responds to demand. Low Latency favors quick response. The hardware disclosure shows what the active mode is doing.

title: Battery and idle settings by power source
caption: The charging limit, display timeout and sleep timeout share one panel. Each timeout can be set independently on battery and while plugged in.

title: To-Do: a new app
