caption: Olo's own to-do app (Ben: "a beautiful olo native todo app that supports reminders / due dates / simple kanban style board / attaching links, images, etc. / beautiful styled deskbar widgets"). Today: what's overdue and what's due, each in its list's colour; the chosen to-do's details at the right, with its reminder, notes and what's attached.

title: To-Do: a list as a board
caption: A lane a section, and a last lane of what's done: cards dragged between them, one dropped on Done checked off.

title: To-Do: a new to-do typed as you'd say it
caption: On a board, a lane's + puts a card there to type in. The words read as its due turn blue as they're typed, the due they say under them as the card will have it, with an × that keeps them as words.

title: To-Do: Upcoming, and a day picked from a month
caption: Upcoming's days as headings; the kit's small month in the details, today outlined and the chosen day filled (Calendar's small month too).

title: To-Do's board in the dark look
Windows snap into place: the places while a window is dragged
caption: Drag a window by its tab and each place it can go has a pad: a plate with a picture of the screen, the place filled in, and a letter's key cap. Q E Z C the quarters, A D and W X the halves, S the whole screen along the top, and one on each other window (the two swap). A letter pressed is the window let go there.

title: Snapping: the window itself is the preview
caption: With the pointer in a pad (A, the left half) the window glides into the place, drawn by its app at every size on the way, and the other pads step back to their letters. Let go and it's tiled there; Escape puts it back.

title: Snapping: another window's place swaps the two
caption: On another window's pad the dragged window takes its place and the other glides to where this one was, glowing as a new window can. By night: the plates a step lighter than the panels, with a bevel that shows.

title: Preferences ▸ Windows: Dragging a Window
caption: The places can be turned off.

title: The window menu, in groups
caption: A tab's right-click menu was twenty-odd items in one list. Now ten in four groups: Hide, Roll Up, Send to Back; Zoom, Float and Tile (its size and shape); Pin, Move and Show (where it is); Close and Quit. Items in a group show their keys of two parts, and every menu's keys stand in a straight column (the last key in a cell).

title: Shortcuts of two parts: the panel while a group waits
caption: Ctrl+Alt+Cmd+Z, F or V begins a group (Zoom, Float, Move); a second key picks from it. Held a third of a second, a panel at the foot of the screen says what each key does; the workspace the window is on is checked. Escape, any other key, a click or five seconds lets go.

title: Preferences, Keyboard, Shortcuts: a second key
caption: Any shortcut can have keys of two parts: click it, type its keys, then Add a Second Key and type the key to press after them. The row last changed stays lit; the note is the list's caption; All Default Keys (it was Default Keys) is at the right.

title: Deskbar's menus, in groups
caption: An application's and a workspace's right-click menus as the window menu is: Show and Hide, Move (workspaces, displays, an agent's screen) and Show on AirPlay with the grouping, Close last; said in the singular for one window.

title: The shortcuts sheet in Russian
caption: Every shortcut's title and group were the protocol's English in every language, on the sheet, in the panel a two-part shortcut waits in, and in Preferences ▸ Keyboard ▸ Shortcuts: 207 titles, now asked for where they're painted and in twelve languages.

title: A shortcut's second key, in Japanese
caption: The panel's rows come from app_server as text and are looked up by what they say.

title: Preferences ▸ Phone's first step, in Russian
caption: The set-up's steps, a device's state and what failed were in no catalog (53 words, with Bluetooth's). Pictured with a made-up phone (OLO_PHONE_DEMO=connect): a test session lists the person's own.

title: A note never ends on one word alone
caption: Wrapping fills each line before the next, which left "tray." and "space." alone under Preferences ▸ Windows' menus and preview. The last word takes the one before it down now, where both fit and the line they leave stays the longer: a rule of the kits' text layout, for every paragraph set to read.

title: Performance ▸ Kernel: Processor Turns and Memory, and a tab that ends on one line
caption: Two settings are new: Keep a busy program's turn short (the scheduler's base slice at 0.7 ms) and Use swap only when nothing else is left (vm.swappiness 0 with the kernel's older reclaim). The six boxes are in two balanced columns (processors and memory left; disks, network, graphics right), every box's facts share one label width and their rows are as far apart as the paragraph's lines, so boxes side by side and both columns end on one line; the note runs across both. Three rounds with Astra and Opus.

title: Performance ▸ Kernel: five boxes, the kernel's settings beside Olo's pieces
caption: The Memory box (Swap used last) is gone: the setting was withdrawn the day it was made. What is left is laid out again: the kernel's own settings on the left (Preemption, Processor Turns, Removable Disks), Olo's pieces in the kernel on the right (Network, Graphics), the columns as far apart as the boxes are from each other, Processor Turns and Graphics ending on one line, and the note that says whose the settings are under the right column, level with the title beside it.

title: Olo Doctor: NVIDIA's driver stuck, and the console that causes it
caption: Two findings new to Doctor (shown in its demo report): NVIDIA's graphics driver stuck shutting down, said as what it is with what it costs until the restart and no fix that could hang; and, recommended, the text console NVIDIA's driver keeps on a card nothing is connected to, with Turn Off the Console. The first points to the second where both are there. Words after both reviewers' looks.

title: Olo Doctor: a fix under way says how it goes
caption: Beside a card's buttons, what its fix is doing and for how long; in the header too; and after three minutes, for a fix run as the administrator, a line of its own: still going, other fixes wait, and what stops it if it never ends. It said only "Fixing…", for hours once.

title: An agent's screen sits still: its Deskbar without the live widgets, its clock without seconds
caption: On a screen nobody sits at, Deskbar shows none of the person's live widgets and its clock has no seconds: they were all that changed on an idle agent's screen, and kept its Deskbar, its app_server and its recorder at work without end (1.9% of a core and 90 wakes a second a screen; 0.1% and 8 now, with the keep-warm frame off there, the recorder looking only at what was drawn, and a status that holds only what the bar draws). On every Deskbar: the tray's well has a point more room above and below its icons (a count's pill came to a pixel of its bevel), the fold button's chevrons end where the time does, and Wi-Fi's tip no longer gives the signal's figure, which is in its menu (it drew the bar again at every waver).

title: Olo Doctor: a driver stuck shutting down, in plainer words
caption: Both reviewers, of the card that says NVIDIA's driver is stuck: 'the kernel', a module's name in the middle of the sentence and 'a processor' made its reader guess. It says Linux, the graphics card, one of the processors, and names the part that is stuck last, in a sentence of its own. And a path through menus (Preferences ▸ Keyboard, in the card under it) no longer breaks beside its arrow, anywhere in Olo.

title: Olo Doctor: NVIDIA's unseen console, said plainly
caption: The card that offers to turn off the console NVIDIA's driver keeps on a card with no screen: what it is and what turning it off does, in words read once (both reviewers: 'giving that console back' and 'the fix has it take no console' read like the code), without the option file's path, and saying when it takes effect. It claims no more than before: one of the steps where the driver can get stuck.

title: Kit: a control that can't be used is dimmed once
caption: Before (left) and after: a disabled check box, button and menu field were dimmed twice (their own grey, then the element layer's fade) and came out fainter than a disabled field beside them; now each is drawn as when enabled and faded once, and the disabled text colour is that same half, so all are one grey. A disabled slider's filled part is the track's grey; a field whose text is wider than it ends in an ellipsis at a whole word while it isn't edited; the example's buttons sit on one middle.

title: Preferences ▸ Performance: what depends on Lower background work sits under it
caption: The note about a terminal's job is right under its check box; the slider and the Background list are set in under the check box's label and greyed together with it off.

title: Preferences ▸ Performance: Give compilers and linkers only spare memory
caption: A new choice under Lower background work: compilers and linkers go in a group of their own inside the login session, kept to the memory nothing else needs (they give theirs up first when it runs short). Off as it comes; there to turn on in a session Olo's login divided.

title: Preferences ▸ Performance: the choice where the session isn't divided
caption: In a session that Olo's login didn't set up for it the choice is greyed, and a line that stays readable says what to do, with Olo Doctor a press away.

title: Preferences ▸ Power: each mode can be changed
caption: Beside the modes, a box for the one in use with everything it sets: a preset and a top speed (100% down to 50%) for the processors and each graphics card, graphics kept ready, fans, the drive, and what the session does. A changed mode says Customized, here and beside its name, and Restore Defaults puts it back.

title: Olo Doctor: the desktop first on the GPU, an account's own choice
caption: Intel's driver puts the window server's drawing ahead of other programs' only where it may set priorities. Doctor offers that for the account, in a card of two paragraphs (what it is for; the permission it takes), with a button of its own: its mark is greyed and says in a tip that it is never fixed with the others. Once given, Doctor's line says what the driver itself answers the window server.

title: Olo Doctor: test desktops still running
caption: A test desktop (a whole headless desktop Olo's development tools start to try something) left running for over an hour is a finding now, with which and for how long, and a fix that ends everything of theirs. A tool's own desktops end with the tool; three had been left for up to two and a half days.

title: Performance ▸ Kernel: a sixth box, Drawing
caption: Olo's module that keeps a program from being held while the graphics driver looks for a 2 MB piece of memory has its box (shown here on a made-up computer with it in force); the box that was Graphics is Window Buffers; each column's last box takes its column's spare height, and the note about whose the settings are runs under both. The module is built and checked, and not offered yet.

title: Olo Doctor: drawing waits for large pieces of graphics memory
caption: The card Olo Doctor will offer once the module has been tried on a real computer (here in its made-up report): what was measured, and what the fix does, in two paragraphs.

title: Terminal: a title without its spinner
caption: A coding agent turns a spinner in its tab's title ten times a second; every frame was a change to the tab, the window's tab, Deskbar and whatever lists windows. The spinner is left out of the title now (here the agent's own words, steady), and the tab's own mark, the blue arc on its icon, says it is working.

title: Tabs end with their strip, to the pixel
caption: Where two folder tabs meet, enlarged: before (left) each tab ran a device pixel past the strip, a tick under every lower corner and a row of the tab behind's colour under the line along the foot; after (right) the outlines end on the line. Found by a reviewer's look at other pictures.

title: Terminal: an agent at work, as a ring on its tab's icon
caption: The mark of a coding agent at work was a three-quarter arc that read as a letter in a still picture. Now a ring drawn on whole pixels as the icons are: faint all the way round, with a strong head and a tail fading behind it, set off from the icon by a rim of the tab's own fill (here on the front tab, enlarged). Five rounds of the two reviewers' looks.

title: Tracker: columns resized by hand
caption: The line between two columns is dragged and every column of every window follows; one width, saved (220 points to start, a double click gives it back). The line is now one line that the rows on both sides meet at every scale, drawn stronger under the pointer.

title: Rex: where a closed terminal was
caption: A session with no terminals, a host with none, a host or the server gone: each says so by name where the terminal would be, with the one thing to do; before, a closed terminal left a dead picture of another session there. The status bar at the bottom is always there (the window's host and session at rest, a passing word when there is one); Rex's own notification cards are gone.

title: Preferences: Rex
caption: A panel for the Rex app in place of its own Settings window: which changes of an agent become notifications, the hosts it knows, and what the sessions of each may do on this computer (nothing until ticked).

title: Rex: Remote Access
caption: One window for reaching this computer's sessions from elsewhere: the checkbox that turns the server's Tailscale on, how it stands (with a light), and a group that keeps its place at every step: nothing to scan yet, the sign-in, the address to pair with. It was a section of the app's own Settings window and a window with a code alone.

title: Rex: the menu bar, on Terminal's model
caption: Rex, Edit, View, Pane, Agents, Settings: every toggle with its check, every item enabled only when it can act, the names saying what they do. The app's own Settings window (eight sections, sixty settings, most with nothing behind them) is gone: hosts, permissions and notices are Preferences ▸ Rex, a window's quick choices its menus.

title: Rex: its keys are Olo's
caption: Rex's command-key shortcuts had never worked (⌘D was the end of the shell, not a split). Its commands now have their keys from the keyboard profile, as Terminal's, shown in its menus and changed in Preferences ▸ Keyboard; a Tabs menu lists the session's tabs with ⌘1 to ⌘9.

title: Rex: a command of your own as a child tab
caption: olo agent start --command: a child tab that runs a command (Build Log), shown for the program it is: Running, the plain terminal icon, its command with its paths cut to their names. The children are their host's now: they run, are watched and answered with no desktop connected, and are all there when it connects.

title: Rex: a tab's tree menu names a command and stops by kind
caption: The tab's tree menu: Build Log is a command, Running; stopping a tab's children says what would be stopped (Stop 2 Subagents and 1 Command…). A menu's label with nothing to its right runs under the detail columns.

title: Alerts stand over their window; Rex's error banner has Try Again
caption: An alert asked for by a menu's command stood in the middle of the screen with no parent: it opens over the window it was asked from now, centred across it. The error banner at Rex's foot offers Try Again at its right edge, under the close box.

title: Rex: a transcript's times and results beside what they are of
caption: Before (above), a turn's time and a tool's result stood at the pane's right edge, a window's width from the name and command they belong to. After (below), each follows what it is of: You 14:52:10; a command, then its check and how long it took. A capped column was tried first and both reviewers took it for a pane that had failed to resize.

title: Layout: every thing stands where its neighbour ends, at every scale
caption: Three pairs, before over after, enlarged: Rex at 1.25x (a row of ground between the tab strip and the header under it, gone), Token Pool at 1.25x (a scroll arrow sitting on its well's frame, now inside it), Tracker at 1.75x (a scroll bar a pixel off its frame, now flush). The layout engine rounded a thing's offset in its parent by itself while sizes were cut to rounded edges: nested a few deep, things stood a pixel or two past where their neighbours ended.

title: A dark menu has an edge on every side
caption: In a dark look a menu's right side and foot had only a nearly black outline, which is no edge on a dark panel: both have an inner line now, a step dimmer than the top and left. Its separators meet the frame at every scale (at 1.5× each end stood a pixel short). Before and after at 1.5×, whole and its corner enlarged.

title: Token Pool: a chosen account's tint runs to its rule
caption: Under a chosen account the tint stopped short of the rule, a strip of the list's ground between them (both reviewers: "end the band exactly on the rule"). The rule is the next row's own top edge now. Before and after, light and dark, at 2× enlarged twice.

title: An Agent Screen on a Rex host itself
caption: A whole Olo desktop of the host's own, drawn in software on a server with no GPU, with no desktop asked: `olo screen install` put Olo and Chrome under the account, `olo screen --on host start` started it, and Chrome shows a page served from the same machine, its button pressed through the tree (`click --role Button --name "Press me"`). The machine's name, under Tracker's disk, is painted out.

title: Rex's Host window: a Screens tab
caption: A host's own Agent Screens from the desktop: Olo and Chrome put on the host, updated and removed here (its line says what is there, what it lacks, which screens run, and how far an install is), and where screens open by default. One round of both reviewers' looks: one structure in every state, both sizes by name, the host's copy never called a desktop, a greyed choice that says why.

title: Rex's Host window: a host's screens, listed
caption: The Screens tab lists a host's own Agent Screens (running first, the newest at the top), shows the one chosen as it is now (a picture brought over the link) and stops it; an install there has a bar for the whole of it and a Cancel that ends it on the host. One round of both reviewers: the list kept in every state, the title the widest column, a failed stop's line in the failures' ink with its room kept.

title: Rex: a host's Tweaks
caption: The Host window has a fifth tab, Tweaks: the machine's own settings, changed as root. The limits that were a page of the Server window moved here (Ben: "they really belong in manage host"), each a line of the window's own grammar with its reason under it and Apply… or Put Back…, with two more: temporary files kept on disk where /tmp is the machine's memory, and brush as the sign-in shell of new accounts.

title: Rex: what a tweak changes, before it is changed
caption: A tweak's question is the tab's page itself, as an alert: what it does, and a table of each thing from what it is now to what it will be. Brush's has a box for the accounts already on the host, each named with the shell it has. It was text in columns in the fixed-width face, in a framed box set on the page (both reviewers' first look).

title: Rex: a floating pane that can be used
caption: A new floating terminal showed but could not be selected, clicked or closed (Ben). It was placed against the whole window, so it ran off the right edge with its one button; presses on it went to the pane under it; it was made without the keyboard; it had no close button; a drag went one step and stopped. Now it stands inside the panes, in the middle; its bar is a pane's own head, with Minimize and Close; a line all round it and a shadow under it; a grip of three ridges in its corner; a press anywhere on it brings it to the front and puts the keyboard in it. Put away, it is its head alone at the panes' foot.

title: Rex: the floating pane in a dark look
caption: The same at 2×, dark: the card's line is a light grey there (the look's control outline is darker than a terminal's ground), so the card stands off the panes under it.

title: Every app's first menu: settings above Keyboard Shortcuts
caption: Under About, the app's settings item now comes first and Keyboard Shortcuts after it (they were the other way round), in every app: Menu::app_items in the kit. Ben: "settings above kb shortcuts in every app's first menu makes sense to me".

title: Rex: Keep It Going and Auto Approve on every agent's row in Activity
caption: Right-clicking any agent in the Activity list now offers Keep It Going and Auto Approve for that row's own pane (a tab's own agent's row had neither; a child's did). Both rows' menus read in one order: what shows, the two switches, what folds, and, apart, what stops.

title: Deskbar's Inbox: Clear All
caption: A third button on the Inbox card's foot clears every notification in the stack that may go (pinned ones and ones that wait for an answer stay), in one step the notifications service can take back. Ben: 'add another icon button for clearing all notifications not just the one on top'.

title: Deskbar's Inbox: what was cleared, and Undo
caption: After Clear All the card says how many went, for eight seconds, with Undo: the service puts back exactly that batch.

title: Rex's Host window: Rex server limits in Tweaks
caption: A tweak that raises a Rex server's own limits (512 tabs a session, 128 panes, 128 sessions, 4,096 blocks; Rex's are 64, 64, 64, 1,024) by a systemd drop-in, written only where Olo is certain of the server's command. No server is restarted: the row says what it has now and what it will have. Ben: 'at least 2x what they are now'.

title: Rex server limits: what will change, and for whom
caption: The confirmation for a shared server says that everyone on the host shares it and that a restart ends the programs in everyone's tabs; a personal server's says whose it is and gives the command to restart it.

title: Screenshot: a card with the picture just taken
caption: After a screenshot its picture comes up in a card at the screen's lower left: drag it out and the file goes with it. Delete, Show in Tracker, Open and Copy; gone twenty seconds after the pointer leaves it, put away before the next shot, never in a picture or a recording. Ben: 'a notification that comes up in the bottom left with a thumbnail … drag and drop … just like in macos'.

title: The card shows a few pixels as blocks, a strip from its start
caption: A picture of a few pixels dragged out of the screen is shown as crisp blocks of whole device pixels, never smoothed; a long strip from its start at its own size, its far end going out into the card with its frame. The frame is always the picture's own edge.
